vehicles.description: What a Ford F-150 costs in November 2026: MSRP by trim, how far under sticker to aim, Ford’s current incentives, and whether to buy new, used or CPO.
vehicles.h1: Ford F-150 price: what to pay and how far under MSRP to aim
vehicles.summary: Reviewers rank the F-150 first among full-size pickups, and right now the one to price is a 2026 XLT. Ford has $4,500 cash on it through November 30 in most regions. Published sale prices put the average XLT or Lariat 5–7% under MSRP before that cash, so on a base XLT the two together take roughly $7,300 off a $47,490 sticker. Watch the options, though. A typical XLT SuperCrew 4x4 on a dealer lot stickers in the mid-$50,000s or higher. The new 2027 has no incentives yet. Prices and offers were checked on November 15, 2026, and your dealer may land a point or two either side of that discount.

after: For 2027, XL, STX and XLT went up. Lariat, Tremor and Raptor went down, but the cheaper Tremor and Raptor lost equipment to get there, so compare window stickers line by line.

pick: A 2026 XLT SuperCrew 4x4. At MSRP it costs $2,840 more than an STX, but in most regions Ford’s $4,500 cash applies to the XLT alone, so it can come out cheaper. It also opens up the options most buyers want, such as a 360-degree camera, heated seats and BlueCruise (hands-free driving on mapped highways). And about half of all used F-150s for sale are XLTs, which makes it the easiest one to sell later.

If you want leather, cooled seats and the 360 camera as standard, the Lariat discounts about as well, though it starts $14,865 higher. We’d skip the PowerBoost hybrid unless you’ll use its onboard generator (outlets in the bed that run tools and appliances). It loses value faster than the gas truck, and Consumer Reports ranked it among its least reliable vehicles in 2022 and 2023.

intro: Ford dealers have more trucks than they want. At the end of September they held 101 days of supply against 82 for the industry, and the 2027s have arrived since, so the 2026s on the lot need to go. TrueCar’s November figures show the average 2026 XLT selling 5.6% under MSRP and the average Lariat 6.5% under. Dealer invoice on an XL sits about 4.5% under MSRP, so expect the least room on the cheapest trucks.

rows.why: Thin margins. Invoice is only about 4.5% below MSRP on these trims.
The most trucks on lots and the most dealers competing for the sale.
Fewer on each lot, so it depends on how long that truck has sat.
Sells at about sticker. Buyers report Raptor R markups of $5,000 and up.

intro: Our take: buy new, and buy the 2026. F-150s hold their value too well for a used one to save much, and used-loan rates run nearly 5 points higher than new.

rows.when: You are financing, or you want an XLT or Lariat. Ford’s offers and the dealer discount stack here.
rows.check: That the truck is a 2026 and not a 2027, and that the offer applies to that exact trim in your ZIP.

rows.check: That it is Gold Certified, not Blue. Gold adds a 12-month, 12,000-mile comprehensive warranty and 7-year, 100,000-mile powertrain coverage. Blue gives 90 days.

rows.when: Your budget is under about $35,000.
rows.check: Open recalls by VIN, and an independent inspection. The 2021 and 2022 trucks have the most recalls of this generation.

after: If you buy used, make 2023 the floor. The 2021 and 2022 trucks carry the most recalls of this generation, including broken intake valves on the 2.7L engine and a failing fuel pump. Drive any used one long enough to feel the 10-speed shift cold and warm.

watch: Dealer add-ons. Bedliners, tint and theft-recovery devices are the dealer’s products, not Ford’s. Refuse or negotiate them.
The model year. A 2026 and a 2027 look alike on the lot. The offers apply only to the 2026.
Rebates dressed up as a discount. Get the selling price first, then each incentive on its own line.
The Ford Credit requirement. Finance elsewhere and the bonus cash tied to 0% or 1.9% goes away.
Fees. Documentation fees differ by hundreds of dollars. Compare out-the-door prices.
Raptor R markups. Owner forums report $5,000 or more over sticker. MSRP is a good result.
faq: Is the Ford F-150 a good truck?

The reviewers think so. Edmunds rates the 2026 an 8.0 out of 10 and first of five large trucks, and U.S. News ranks it first of six full-size pickups. The weak spots are owner complaints about harsh shifts from the 10-speed automatic and a long recall list on 2021 and 2022 trucks.
How much under MSRP can you get a Ford F-150?

On a 2026 XLT or Lariat, 5–7% under MSRP is a fair deal before Ford’s cash and about 10% is a strong one. XL and STX have less room, around 2–3%. Raptors sell at about sticker. Those ranges are our read of TrueCar’s November sale prices, so a given dealer may land a point or two either side. The averages may already include Ford’s cash, so count the cash as extra only when the quote shows it on its own line.
Should I buy a 2026 or a 2027 F-150?

The 2026, for most buyers. It carries Ford’s year-end offers and dealers want it gone now that 2027s are arriving. The 2027 makes sense if you want the new 3.0L engine or the lower starting price on Lariat, Tremor or Raptor.
What is the destination charge on an F-150?
$2,795 on most 2026 trucks and on the 2027. Ford’s advertised starting prices leave it out, and it is on every window sticker. A few early 2026 trucks show $2,595.
Can I combine 0% financing with the $4,500 cash back?
Plan on no. Ford’s 0% and 1.9% offers come with $500 or $1,500 in bonus cash, and the full $4,500 appears only as a cash offer. Ask the dealer to price the truck both ways in writing.
Is the F-150 hybrid worth it?

Only if you will use the onboard generator. It loses value faster than the gas truck by iSeeCars’ figures, and the early hybrids scored poorly for reliability with Consumer Reports. Consumer Reports now predicts about average reliability for the 2026.
Is a used F-150 a better deal than new?

Not by much right now. A three-year-old F-150 has lost about 19% of its value, against 25% for the average vehicle, and used loans averaged 11.19% in the second quarter of 2026 against 6.35% for new. The new 2026 also has 0% financing or cash back. A Gold Certified 2023 or 2024 is the used route we’d take.

vehicles.title: Toyota RAV4 Price: MSRP, Discounts and What to Pay | Steer Me Right
vehicles.description: What a Toyota RAV4 costs in November 2026: MSRP by trim for 2026 and 2027, how close to sticker dealers sell it, Toyota’s current offers, and whether to buy new, used or CPO.
vehicles.h1: Toyota RAV4 price: what to pay and how far under MSRP to aim
vehicles.summary: The RAV4 is hybrid-only now, and it’s still one of the easiest small SUVs to recommend: 43 mpg combined with front-wheel drive, an owner score of 85 out of 100 from J.D. Power, and a three-year depreciation rate about half the average vehicle’s. The catch is the price. Dealers had 24 days of RAV4s in stock at the end of October against 87 for the industry, Toyota offers no cash back, and TrueCar’s November averages put most trims within 2% of sticker. Price a 2026 XLE Premium, aim for 1–2% under MSRP, and take Toyota’s 4.99% financing if your bank can’t beat it. Prices and offers were checked on November 15, 2026.

after: For 2027, every trim goes up $400 to $755, and AWD goes from $1,400 to $1,600. Every 2027 plug-in gets DC fast charging, an 11-kW onboard charger and a NACS (Tesla-style) charging port, and the Woodland gets retuned suspension with 9.1 inches of ground clearance.

pick: A 2026 XLE Premium, with AWD if you see snow. At $36,100 it costs $1,400 more than an SE and adds the things you notice every day: a power liftgate, SofTex (synthetic leather) heated front seats, and front and rear parking sensors that brake the car if you’re about to back into something. Edmunds calls it the pick of the lineup too, and TrueCar lists it as the most popular trim. AWD adds $1,400 and costs 2 mpg (41 combined against 43).

Skip the Woodland unless you want its all-terrain tires: it starts $3,800 above a front-drive XLE Premium and is rated 38 mpg combined. The plug-in hybrid makes sense only if you can charge at home. An SE plug-in costs $5,400 more than an AWD hybrid SE, the federal tax credit is gone, and Toyota recalled the 2026 plug-ins for a loss of power at highway speed (a software fix). If you do want one, its 54-mile EPA electric range covers most commutes, and the 2027 brings DC fast charging to every plug-in trim.

intro: RAV4s are scarce. Cox Automotive counted 24 days of supply at the end of October, against 39 for Toyota as a whole and 87 for the industry. TrueCar’s November averages show the LE and SE selling about 1.5% under MSRP, the XLE Premium about 1% under, and the Woodland and XSE a little over sticker. Edmunds’ suggested prices, based on Texas sales, run 2–3.4% under.

intro: Our take: buy new, and buy the 2026. A used RAV4 Hybrid barely costs less, and used-loan rates average 11.19% against Toyota’s 4.99% on a new one.

rows.when: Most buyers. Toyota’s 4.99% and the $500 rebates apply only to the 2026.
rows.check: That the SUV is a 2026 and not a 2027, and that the offer runs in your region.

rows.when: You want a plug-in with DC fast charging, or the Woodland’s retuned suspension.
rows.check: The $400 to $755 price rise, and that there are no offers yet.

rows.when: You want a 2023 to 2025 hybrid with a warranty, and you’re paying cash.
rows.check: That it’s Gold Certified, not Silver. Gold adds a 12-month/12,000-mile comprehensive warranty and 7-year/100,000-mile powertrain coverage; Silver gives 12 months of powertrain cover only. The hybrid battery stays covered for 10 years/150,000 miles from first sale.

rows.when: Your budget is under about $28,000.
rows.check: Open recalls by VIN, an independent inspection, and on a 2019 to 2022 AWD hybrid, the high-voltage cables under the floor.

after: If you buy used, make 2023 the floor. The 2019 to 2021 RAV4s carry the most recalls of the last generation, AWD hybrids from 2019 to 2022 can corrode their high-voltage cables, and some hybrids’ fuel tanks won’t fill to the rated 14.5 gallons (a settlement extended that coverage to 15 years/150,000 miles).

watch: Dealer add-ons. Toyota dealers put add-ons on 37.7% of the quotes CarWhere studied, averaging $1,637. Paint protection, nitrogen and etched VINs are the dealer’s products. Refuse or negotiate them.
Markups. Some dealers added $1,104 to $4,700 over sticker when the 2026 launched. Supply is still tight, so walk away from a markup and ask the next dealer.
The model year. A 2026 and a 2027 look alike on the lot. The offers apply only to the 2026.
The Toyota Financial Services requirement. The 4.99% and the $500 rebates need Toyota’s own financing. Compare the total cost with your bank’s rate.
Fees. Documentation fees on RAV4 quotes ran from $180 in Iowa to $1,094 in Florida in CarEdge’s study. Compare out-the-door prices.
The plug-in recall. Ask the dealer to show that recall 26V659’s software update is done before you take delivery.
faq: Is the Toyota RAV4 a good SUV?

Most reviewers think so. Edmunds rates the 2026 an 8.1 out of 10 and third of 12 small hybrid SUVs, and J.D. Power’s owner score of 85 ties it for first among compact SUVs. U.S. News is cooler, at 8.3 and 14th of 19 hybrid SUVs, and calls the drive listless. A three-year-old RAV4 Hybrid has lost 13.8% of its value by iSeeCars’ figures, against 24.8% for the average vehicle.
How much under MSRP can you get a Toyota RAV4?

On a 2026 LE, SE or XLE Premium, 1–2% under MSRP is a fair deal and 3–4% is a strong one. The Woodland, XSE and Limited sell at about sticker. Plug-ins have a little more room, around 2–3%. Those ranges are our read of TrueCar’s November averages and Edmunds’ suggested prices, so a given dealer may land a point either side, and Toyota has no cash back to add on top.
Should I buy a 2026 or a 2027 RAV4?

The 2026, for most buyers. It costs $400 to $755 less, and Toyota’s 4.99% financing and the $500 military and college rebates apply only to the 2026. Wait for the 2027 if you want a plug-in with DC fast charging or the Woodland’s retuned suspension. 2027 hybrids reach dealers late in 2026 and plug-ins early in 2027.
What is the destination charge on a RAV4?
$1,595 on the 2026 and the 2027, hybrid or plug-in. Toyota’s advertised starting prices leave it out, and Toyota says it may differ in AL, AR, FL, GA, LA, MS, NC, OK, SC and TX.
Does Toyota offer cash back on the RAV4?

No. In Chicago, Dallas, Los Angeles and New York on November 15, 2026, Toyota offered 4.99% financing for 48 months and lease deals, but no customer cash. The only money off is a $500 military or college rebate when you finance or lease through Toyota Financial Services.
Is the RAV4 plug-in hybrid worth it?

Only if you can charge at home and most of your trips are short. The SE is EPA-rated for 54 miles on electricity, and Edmunds got 58 in its testing. But it costs $5,400 more than an AWD hybrid SE, and the federal tax credit doesn’t apply to cars bought after September 30, 2025.
Is a used RAV4 a better deal than new?

Rarely. CarWhere’s median asking price for a used 2025 is $32,299, and TrueCar’s average paid for a new 2026 LE is $32,951. Used loans averaged 11.19% in the second quarter of 2026, against Toyota’s 4.99% on a new one. A Gold Certified 2023 to 2025 hybrid is the used route we’d take.

vehicles.name: Honda CR-V
vehicles.title: Honda CR-V Price: MSRP, Discounts and What to Pay | Steer Me Right
vehicles.description: What a Honda CR-V costs in November 2026: MSRP by trim for 2026 and 2027, how far under sticker dealers sell it, Honda’s current offers, and whether to buy new, used or CPO.
vehicles.h1: Honda CR-V price: what to pay and how far under MSRP to aim
vehicles.summary: Honda says the CR-V is America’s best-selling SUV this year, and it’s one of the easier small SUVs to buy below sticker. A 2026 starts at $30,920 with the gas engine and $35,630 as a hybrid, and the 2027 now on Honda’s site is the same car for $400 to $600 more. Dealers had 43 days of CR-Vs in stock at the end of October, against 24 for the RAV4, and verified buyers on CarWhere paid a median 5.7% under MSRP. Price a 2026 Sport Hybrid, aim for 2–5% under, and check Honda’s financing on a 2027 before you sign. Prices and offers were checked on November 16, 2026.

rows.name: LX
rows.gets: 9-inch touchscreen with wireless CarPlay and Android Auto, wireless charger, adaptive cruise and lane keeping

rows.name: EX
rows.gets: Blind-spot monitoring, heated front seats, power moonroof, 18-inch alloys, remote start

rows.name: EX-L
rows.gets: Leather, power tailgate, 10.2-inch digital gauges, parking sensors that brake for you

rows.name: Sport Hybrid
rows.gets: The EX’s equipment with the hybrid, 40 mpg combined, black 18-inch wheels. Cloth seats

rows.name: Sport-L Hybrid
rows.gets: Leather, power tailgate, 10.2-inch digital gauges, parking sensors that brake for you

rows.name: TrailSport Hybrid
rows.gets: All-terrain tires, heated steering wheel, power tailgate, orange trim

rows.name: Sport Touring Hybrid
rows.gets: 19-inch wheels, 12-speaker Bose audio, Google built-in, hands-free tailgate

after: For 2027, the LX goes up $600, every other trim $400, and the destination charge from $1,450 to $1,550. Nothing else changes. AWD adds $1,500 on every trim that offers front drive. Honda says an all-new, hybrid-only CR-V arrives in 2027 as a 2028 model.

pick: A 2026 Sport Hybrid, with AWD if you see snow. At $35,630 it costs $230 more than a gas EX-L and has everything the EX does, including heated front seats, a power moonroof and blind-spot monitoring. In place of the 190-hp turbo it has the 204-hp hybrid, with 247 lb-ft of torque against 179, and it’s rated 40 mpg combined against 30. AWD adds $1,500 and drops it to 37 mpg.

Want leather and a power tailgate? The Sport-L Hybrid adds both, plus parking sensors that brake for you, for $3,095 more, and it’s Edmunds’ pick among the hybrids. Skip the TrailSport unless you want its all-terrain tires: it’s AWD only and rated 35 mpg. If you’d rather have gas, Edmunds picks the EX-L, but the Sport Hybrid costs almost the same.

intro: CR-Vs aren’t scarce. Cox Automotive counted 43 days of supply at the end of October, against 24 for the RAV4 and 87 for the industry, and 2027s were already 43.6% of Honda’s stock. TrueCar’s November averages put the 2026 at 1.6% to 4.9% under sticker by trim, Edmunds’ suggested prices near Austin run 4.8% to 6.4% under, and CarWhere’s verified buyers paid a median 5.7% under.

rows.why: TrueCar averages about 2.9% under. Dealer invoice sits 4–5% under MSRP.
The hybrids sell closest to sticker: TrueCar averages 1.6–1.8% under.
TrueCar averages 3.6–4.9% under. Edmunds suggests 5.7–6.4%.

choice.title: 4.49% costs about {gap} less than the average loan
choice.text: Each bar is how much less you pay in total than at the 6.35% average new-car rate, on a $37,000 CR-V over 60 months. Borrowers with top credit averaged 4.41%, so get your bank’s rate before you sign. Honda’s rate is 4.99% in some regions, and only on a 2027.

intro: Our take: buy new, and price both model years. A leftover 2026 is the same car for $400 to $600 less, but Honda’s low rates are only on the 2027. A used CR-V barely costs less than a new one, and used-loan rates average 11.19%.

rows.when: You find one at 5% or more under MSRP, or you’re paying cash or bringing your own loan.
rows.check: That it’s a 2026, which Honda’s rates and leases don’t cover, and that the price beats a 2027 on Honda’s rate in total.

rows.when: You’ll finance through Honda at 3.49% to 4.99%, or you want the widest choice of trims and colors.
rows.check: The $400 to $600 price rise and the $1,550 destination charge.

rows.when: You want the all-new, hybrid-only CR-V Honda promises for 2027.
rows.check: Honda hasn’t given a price or an on-sale date.

rows.when: You want a 2023 to 2025 with a warranty, and you’re paying cash.
rows.check: HondaTrue Certified covers 2021 and newer cars under 80,000 miles: the powertrain to 7 years/100,000 miles from first sale, everything else 2 years past the new-car warranty. The hybrid battery is covered 8 years/100,000 miles from first sale.

rows.when: Your budget is under about $27,000.
rows.check: Open recalls by VIN, an independent inspection, and on a 2023 to 2025, that steering recall 24V744 is done.

after: If you buy used, make 2023 the floor. That year began the current CR-V, and NHTSA still has an open investigation into 2017 to 2022 CR-Vs that brake hard on their own, with 1,294 owner complaints. The 2017 and 2018 turbo engines could also dilute their oil with fuel, and Honda’s extended warranty on that has run out.

watch: Dealer add-ons. Honda dealers put add-ons on 35.1% of the quotes CarWhere studied, averaging $1,159. Paint protection, nitrogen and etched VINs are the dealer’s products. Refuse or negotiate them.
The model year. A 2026 and a 2027 look the same on the lot. Honda’s rates and leases apply only to the 2027, and the 2026 should cost less.
The Honda Financial Services requirement. The low rates and every $500 or $750 offer need Honda’s own financing. Compare the total cost with your bank’s rate.
“No payments for 90 days.” Interest still builds during those 90 days, so it isn’t a discount.
Fees. CarEdge puts the national median for dealer fees at $498. Compare out-the-door prices, not monthly payments.
Recalls on a used one. On a 2023 to 2025 CR-V, ask for proof that steering recall 24V744 is done.
faq: Is the Honda CR-V a good SUV?

Most reviewers think so. U.S. News scores the 2026 a 9.0 out of 10 and Kelley Blue Book 4.8 out of 5. Edmunds is cooler, at 7.4 (7.7 for the hybrid), and faults the slow gas engine and short list of driver aids. J.D. Power owners give it 82 out of 100. A three-year-old CR-V has lost 13.7% of its value by iSeeCars’ figures, against 24.8% for the average vehicle, and Kelley Blue Book named it the 2026 best resale value compact SUV.
How much under MSRP can you get a Honda CR-V?

On a 2026 LX, EX or EX-L, 3–4% under MSRP is a fair deal and 5–6% a strong one. The Sport and TrailSport hybrids sell closer to sticker, at 2–3%, and the Sport-L and Sport Touring have the most room, at 4–5% or more. Those ranges are our read of TrueCar’s and Edmunds’ November figures and CarWhere’s buyer reports, so a given dealer may land a point either side.
Should I buy a 2026 or a 2027 CR-V?

Price both. Honda changed only the price for 2027: $600 more on the LX, $400 on the rest, and $100 more for destination. A leftover 2026 should cost less, but Honda’s 3.49% to 4.99% financing and its leases are only on the 2027, so compare the total cost of each.
Should I wait for the 2028 CR-V?
Only if you want the new one. Honda says an all-new, hybrid-only CR-V arrives in 2027, but it hasn’t given a price or a date. The current CR-V is a known car that dealers are discounting now.
What is the destination charge on a CR-V?
$1,450 on the 2026 and $1,550 on the 2027. Honda’s advertised starting prices leave it out, and premium paint adds $455.
Does Honda offer cash back on the CR-V?

No. In Chicago, Dallas, Los Angeles and New York on November 16, 2026, Honda offered financing from 3.49%, leases from $299 a month and $500 for current Honda owners, all on the 2027, but no customer cash. Military members and recent graduates get $500 off a 2026 or 2027 when they finance or lease through Honda.
Is the CR-V Hybrid worth it?

For most buyers, yes. The Sport Hybrid costs $230 more than a gas EX-L, makes 204 hp against 190, and is rated 40 mpg combined against 30 with front-wheel drive. You give up the EX-L’s leather and power tailgate. It loses value a little faster: 15.9% in three years against 13.7% for the gas CR-V.
Is a used CR-V a better deal than new?

Rarely. CarWhere’s median asking price for a used 2025 is $33,066, more than TrueCar’s $31,517 average paid for a new 2026 LX. Used loans averaged 11.19% in the second quarter of 2026. A HondaTrue Certified 2023 to 2025 is the used route we’d take.

vehicles.h1: GMC Sierra 1500 price: what to pay and how far under MSRP to aim
vehicles.summary: The 2026 Sierra 1500 is the outgoing truck, and that’s the best reason to buy one now. GMC is already selling an all-new 2027, GMC dealers had 110 days of stock at the end of October against 87 for the industry, and TrueCar’s averages put the SLT and Denali about 7.5% under sticker. You get a roomy, well-finished crew cab and a choice of four engines, including a diesel rated 24 mpg combined. You give up some ride comfort (reviewers rate the Ram 1500’s better), and crash results that trail the class: IIHS rates the crew cab Marginal in its small overlap front test. Price a 2026 SLT crew cab with the 5.3L V8, aim for 5–7% under MSRP, and look at the diesel if you tow, since it’s the only engine GMC puts cash on this month. Prices and offers were checked on November 16, 2026.

after: For 2027 the Sierra is all new: 5.7-liter and 6.6-liter V8s replace the 5.3L and 6.2L, every engine gets a 10-speed automatic, the cabin is redesigned, and the SLE and SLT are dropped. The Pro goes up $700 and the Denali $4,800. Destination is $2,795 on both years.

pick: A 2026 SLT crew cab with the 5.3L V8, with 4WD if you need it. At $55,400 it starts $4,600 above an Elevation, but the Elevation starts as a double cab with the 2.7-liter turbo four. The SLT comes as a crew cab with the V8, a 10-speed automatic, leather and 10-way power front seats. It’s also gone for 2027, along with the SLE, and TrueCar’s averages show SLTs selling about 7.5% under MSRP, with the Denali the deepest discount of any trim.

If you tow often or drive long highway miles, get the 3.0-liter Duramax diesel. It’s rated 24 mpg combined with 4WD against 16 for the 5.3L, and it’s the only engine GMC puts money on this month: $8,250 cash, or 0% for 60 months plus $2,000. Skip the 6.2L V8 for now. NHTSA has an open investigation into failures of GM’s 6.2-liter that covers 2021 to 2026 trucks, including ones already fixed under a 2025 recall. The Denali is the step up for a nicer cabin; the AT4X is for serious off-roading and costs $24,500 more than an SLT.

intro: Our take: buy new, and buy the 2026. Sierras lose value faster than the average pickup, which makes a used one tempting, but a 2026 sells 5–7% under sticker this month and used loans average 11.19% against 6.35% for new.

after: If you buy used, make 2023 the floor. The 2019 and 2020 Sierras carry 10 and 12 recalls, 2021 to 2024 trucks with the 6.2L V8 were recalled in 2025 for crankshaft and connecting-rod defects that can wreck the engine, and owners are suing GM over lifter failures on its V8s.

watch: Which engine. GMC’s cash and 0% apply only to the 3.0L Duramax. Make sure a quote names the engine before you compare it with an ad.
Cash or 0%. On the diesel you get one or the other. Work out the total cost of each with your bank’s rate before you choose.
Dealer add-ons. GMC dealers put add-ons on 36.4% of the quotes CarWhere studied, averaging $1,441. Paint protection, nitrogen and etched VINs are the dealer’s products. Refuse or negotiate them.
Fees. Documentation fees run from about $85 in California to $999 in Florida, by CarEdge’s count. Compare out-the-door prices.
The 6.2L V8. On a 2021 to 2024 truck, ask for proof that recall 25V274’s inspection was done. NHTSA’s open investigation also covers 2025 and 2026 engines.
The transfer case recall. A few 2026 4WD trucks are under recall 26V289 and shouldn’t be driven until fixed. Have the dealer check the VIN before delivery.
faq: Is the GMC Sierra 1500 a good truck?

Reviewers split on it. U.S. News scores the 2026 a 9.0 out of 10, tied for third of six full-size pickups, and Kelley Blue Book gives it 4.3 out of 5. Edmunds is cooler, at 6.7 and fifth of large trucks, faulting the ride and fuel economy. Consumer Reports expects it to be less reliable than the average new car, and iSeeCars finds it loses 27.8% of its value in three years, against 23.7% for full-size pickups.
How much under MSRP can you get a GMC Sierra 1500?

On a 2026 SLE, Elevation or SLT, 5–7% under MSRP is a fair deal and 8–10% a strong one. Denali, AT4 and AT4X trucks sit at 5–7%, and the Pro has less room, about 2–3%. Those ranges are our read of TrueCar’s market averages and iSeeCars’ invoice figures, and GMC’s diesel cash comes on top.
Should I buy a 2026 or a 2027 Sierra 1500?

The 2026, unless you want the new truck. It costs less (the Denali starts $4,800 lower), the SLE and SLT exist only as 2026s, and GMC’s cash and 0% offers are on the 2026 diesel. The 2027 brings 5.7L and 6.6L V8s, a 10-speed automatic on every engine and a redesigned cabin, but GMC lists just one lease offer on it so far.
What is the destination charge on a Sierra 1500?
$2,795 on the 2026 and the 2027. GMC’s advertised starting prices leave it out.
Does GMC offer cash back on the Sierra 1500?

Only on the diesel. On November 16, 2026, GMC offered $8,250 ($6,250 plus $2,000 bonus cash) on a 2026 Sierra 1500 with the 3.0L Duramax, or 0% for 60 months plus $2,000, in Chicago, Dallas, Los Angeles and New York. Gas 2026 trucks got lease deals only. The offers end November 30.
Is the Sierra’s 6.2L V8 reliable?

It has a record. GM recalled nearly 600,000 2021 to 2024 trucks and SUVs with the 6.2L in 2025 for crankshaft and connecting-rod defects that can cause engine failure, and NHTSA has since opened a wider investigation covering 2021 to 2026 engines, including ones already fixed. Until that closes, we’d take the 5.3L V8 or the diesel.
Is the Sierra 1500 the same truck as the Silverado?

They’re closely related and offer the same four engines. The Sierra costs more (the 2026 Pro starts at $38,600, against $37,200 for a Silverado WT) and is finished a step higher inside. With the two this close, price both and let the better deal decide.

vehicles.h1: Chevrolet Silverado 1500 price: what to pay and how far under MSRP to aim
vehicles.summary: The 2026 Silverado 1500 is the outgoing truck, and Chevrolet is paying you to take one. Dealers had 99 days of Silverados at the end of October against 87 for the industry, and Chevrolet has $6,000 cash on V8 models or 0% for 60 months, both for delivery by November 30. You get a full-size crew cab from $37,200, four engines including a diesel rated up to 25 mpg combined, and up to 13,300 pounds of towing. You give up ride and cabin polish (Edmunds scores the 2026 an average 6.1 out of 10), crash results that trail the class (IIHS rates the crew cab Poor in its updated moderate overlap test), and Consumer Reports expects below-average reliability. The all-new 2027 is a clearly better truck by Edmunds’ score (7.7, second of five large trucks), but it costs $900 to $8,500 more on most trims and Chevrolet lists no offers on it yet. Price a 2026 LT crew cab with the 5.3L V8, aim for 5–7% under MSRP on top of the $6,000, and take the 0% instead if you finance. Prices and offers were checked on November 16, 2026.

after: For 2027 the Silverado is all new: 5.7-liter and 6.6-liter V8s replace the 5.3L and 6.2L, every engine gets a 10-speed automatic, and a 16.3-inch screen is standard. The RST and LTZ are dropped, the LT becomes the “Silverado” (Z71 on every 4WD) and the LT Trail Boss becomes the Trail Boss. The High Country rises $8,500 and the ZR2 $5,400. Destination is $2,795 on both years. Chevrolet lists up to 13,300 pounds of towing on the 2026 and 13,700 on the 2027 with the 5.7L.

pick: A 2026 LT crew cab with the 5.3L V8, with 4WD if you need it. At $48,200 it starts $3,100 below an RST, and it has the 13.4-inch touchscreen and 12.3-inch digital gauges. The 5.3L is the engine Chevrolet puts $6,000 on this month; an LT with the TurboMax four gets $2,250. TrueCar’s averages show LTs selling about 5% under MSRP, so there’s room to ask for more, and the RST’s black-wheel look is the one to haggle on, since those average nearly 7% under.

If you tow often or drive long highway miles, get the 3.0-liter Duramax diesel. It’s rated up to 25 mpg combined (23 to 24 with 4WD) against 17 for the 5.3L, and a 2026 can tow up to 13,300 pounds. Chevrolet puts no cash on it this month, so expect to pay more for it. Skip the 6.2L V8 for now. NHTSA has an open investigation into failures of GM’s 6.2-liter that covers 2021 to 2026 trucks, including ones already fixed under a 2025 recall. The High Country is the step up for a nicer cabin; the ZR2 is for serious off-roading and costs $23,600 more than an LT.

intro: Our take: buy new. The 2026 for the price, the 2027 if you want the better truck. Silverados lose value faster than the average pickup, which makes a used one tempting, but a 2026 sells 5–7% under sticker this month with $6,000 cash or 0% on top, and used loans average 11.19% against 6.35% for new.

rows.when: Most buyers. The runout discounts and Chevrolet’s cash and 0% are on the 2026, and the RST and LTZ exist only as 2026s.
rows.check: That the truck is a 2026, which engine it has (the $6,000 needs the 5.3L), and that the offer runs in your region.

rows.when: You want the new 5.7L or 6.6L V8, the 16.3-inch screen and the redesigned cabin, or the 13,700-pound tow rating. Edmunds scores it 7.7 against 6.1 for the 2026.
rows.check: The price rise ($8,500 on the High Country, $900 to $1,400 on the Custom and WT), and that Chevrolet lists no 2027 offers yet.

rows.when: You want a 2023 to 2025 truck with some cover, and you’re paying cash.
rows.check: CarBravo’s certified warranty is 12 months/12,000 miles bumper to bumper on trucks under 10 model years and 100,000 miles. Chevrolet’s powertrain warranty runs 5 years/60,000 miles from first sale.

rows.when: Your budget is under about $37,000.
rows.check: Open recalls by VIN, an independent inspection, and on a 6.2L V8, proof that recall 25V274’s engine inspection was done.

after: If you buy used, make 2023 the floor. The 2019 and 2020 Silverados carry 10 and 12 recalls, 2021 to 2024 trucks with the 6.2L V8 were recalled in 2025 for crankshaft and connecting-rod defects that can wreck the engine, and owners are suing GM over lifter failures on its V8s.

watch: Which engine. Chevrolet’s $6,000 applies only to the 5.3L V8 and the $2,250 only to an LT with the TurboMax. Make sure a quote names the engine before you compare it with an ad.
Cash or 0%. You get one or the other. Work out the total cost of each with your bank’s rate before you choose.

Dealer add-ons. Chevrolet dealers put add-ons on 32.4% of the quotes CarWhere studied, averaging $1,443. Paint protection, nitrogen and etched VINs are the dealer’s products. Refuse or negotiate them.
Fees. Documentation fees run from about $85 in California to $999 in Florida, by CarEdge’s count. Compare out-the-door prices.
The 6.2L V8. On a 2021 to 2024 truck, ask for proof that recall 25V274’s inspection was done. NHTSA’s open investigation also covers 2025 and 2026 engines.
The transfer case recall. A few 2026 4WD trucks are under recall 26V289, and GM tells owners not to drive them until fixed. Have the dealer check the VIN before delivery.
faq: Is the Chevrolet Silverado 1500 a good truck?

Reviewers are lukewarm on the 2026 and warmer on the 2027. U.S. News scores the 2026 an 8.8 out of 10, fifth of six full-size pickups, Kelley Blue Book gives it 4.3 out of 5, and J.D. Power gives it 82 out of 100, tied for third among large light-duty pickups. Edmunds is cooler on the 2026, at 6.1, but rates the redesigned 2027 a 7.7 and second of five large trucks. Consumer Reports expects the 2026 to be less reliable than the average new car, and iSeeCars finds it loses 30.4% of its value in three years, against 23.7% for full-size pickups.
How much under MSRP can you get a Chevrolet Silverado 1500?

On a 2026 LT, RST, Custom Trail Boss, LTZ or LT Trail Boss, 5–7% under MSRP is a fair deal and 8–10% a strong one. High Country and ZR2 trucks sit at 5–7%, and the WT and Custom have less room, about 2–3%. Those ranges are our read of TrueCar’s market averages and iSeeCars’ invoice figures, and Chevrolet’s cash comes on top.
Should I buy a 2026 or a 2027 Silverado 1500?

The 2026 if price matters most. It costs less (the High Country starts $8,500 lower), the RST and LTZ exist only as 2026s, and Chevrolet’s cash and 0% offers are on the 2026. The 2027 brings 5.7L and 6.6L V8s, a 10-speed automatic on every engine and a redesigned cabin, and Edmunds scores it 7.7 against 6.1 for the 2026, but we found no Chevrolet offer on it yet.
What is the destination charge on a Silverado 1500?
$2,795 on the 2026 and the 2027. Chevrolet’s advertised starting prices leave it out.
Does Chevrolet offer cash back on the Silverado 1500?

Yes, on the V8. On November 16, 2026, Chevrolet offered $6,000 ($4,250 plus $1,750 bonus cash) on a 2026 Silverado 1500 with the 5.3L V8 and $2,250 on an LT with the TurboMax, or 0% for 60 months, in Chicago, Dallas, Los Angeles and New York. The cash can’t be combined with special financing or a lease, and all of it ends with delivery by November 30.
Is the Silverado’s 6.2L V8 reliable?

It has a record. GM recalled nearly 600,000 2021 to 2024 trucks and SUVs with the 6.2L in 2025 for crankshaft and connecting-rod defects that can cause engine failure, and NHTSA has since opened a wider investigation covering 2021 to 2026 engines, including ones already fixed. Until that closes, we’d take the 5.3L V8 or the diesel.
How much can a Silverado 1500 tow?

Chevrolet lists up to 13,300 pounds on the 2026 and up to 13,700 on the 2027 with the new 5.7L V8. The 2026 diesel is the one it advertises for the 13,300 figure; what a specific truck can tow depends on its engine, cab, axle ratio and hitch, so check the trailering rating on the truck’s own label.
Is the Silverado 1500 the same truck as the Sierra?

They’re closely related and offer the same four engines. The Silverado costs less (the 2026 WT starts at $37,200, against $38,600 for a Sierra Pro) and is finished a step lower inside. Chevrolet puts its November cash on the V8, so price both and let the better deal decide.

vehicles.description: What a Toyota Tacoma costs in November 2026: MSRP by trim for 2026 and 2027, how far under sticker dealers sell it, Toyota’s current offers, and whether to buy new, used or CPO.
vehicles.h1: Toyota Tacoma price: what to pay and how far under MSRP to aim
vehicles.summary: The Tacoma is the midsize pickup that holds its value best: Kelley Blue Book named it the best-resale midsize pickup of 2026, and iSeeCars puts its five-year depreciation at 19.5% against 30.2% for the class. It isn’t the roomiest or quietest truck you can buy. Edmunds ranks it third of seven midsize trucks, and both Edmunds and U.S. News fault the tight back seat. It does sell under sticker, though: CarWhere’s 31 verified 2026 buyers paid a median 7.9% under MSRP, and TrueCar’s averages put the SR5 and TRD Sport 5–6% under. Price a 2026 TRD Sport, aim for 5–6% under MSRP, and take Toyota’s 3.99% financing if your bank can’t beat it. Prices and offers were checked on November 16, 2026.

after: Prices leave out the $1,745 destination charge. For 2027, every trim goes up $180 except the TRD Sport and TRD Off-Road, which go up $520. Toyota lists the same 11 trims for 2027.

pick: A 2026 TRD Sport Double Cab, with 4x4 if you leave pavement. At $40,415 it adds a sport-tuned suspension and 18-inch TRD wheels to the SR5’s 278-hp engine, and Edmunds found it rides more smoothly than the TRD Off-Road. Edmunds calls it the pick of the lineup too, and TrueCar’s averages show it selling 5.7% under sticker, more than any other trim. 4x4 adds $3,200 with the automatic, and the 6-speed manual on the 4x4 costs $800 less than that.

If you’ll use trails, a TRD Off-Road costs only $300 more than a TRD Sport 4x4 automatic ($43,915 against $43,615) and adds Bilstein shocks with remote reservoirs, a locking rear differential and Crawl Control (a low-speed cruise control for rough ground). Skip the i-FORCE MAX hybrid unless you want its torque or its 2,400-watt outlet: it adds $3,720 to a TRD Sport 4x4, is rated 23 mpg combined against 21, and doesn’t raise the Tacoma’s 6,500-pound maximum towing. The Trailhunter and TRD Pro start above $63,000 and get none of Toyota’s current offers.

intro: Tacomas sell quickly but not at sticker. Edmunds says new ones are selling in about 18 days against 34 for the average new vehicle, and Toyota had 39 days of supply at the end of October against 87 for the industry. Buyers still get real money off: CarWhere’s 31 verified 2026 buyers paid a median 7.9% under MSRP, Edmunds’ suggested prices, based on Texas sales, run 6–7% under, and TrueCar’s averages put the SR5, PreRunner and TRD Sport 5–6% under. The base SR and the TRD Pro have the least room.

rows.when: Most buyers. Toyota’s financing, leases and the SR5 cash apply to the 2026, and it costs $180 to $520 less than a 2027.
rows.check: That the truck is a 2026 and not a 2027, and that the offer runs in your region.

rows.check: That it’s Gold Certified, not Silver. Gold adds a 12-month/12,000-mile comprehensive warranty and 7-year/100,000-mile powertrain coverage; Silver gives 12 months of powertrain cover only. An i-FORCE MAX hybrid battery stays covered for 10 years/150,000 miles from first sale.

rows.check: Open recalls by VIN, an independent inspection, and on a 2022 or 2023, that the rear axle recall is done.

after: If you buy a 2024 or 2025, get the recall work in writing. The first two years of this generation were recalled for rear brake hoses, shock-absorber reservoirs and the dashboard warning display, and Toyota replaced some 2024 automatic transmissions under a service bulletin. On a 2022 or 2023, the rear axle shafts were recalled because they could separate.

watch: Add-ons. In Florida, Georgia, Alabama and the Carolinas, Toyota’s regional distributor fits its own packages before the truck reaches the dealer; one 2026 buyer reported $2,857 of them plus $1,599 from the dealer. Refuse or negotiate anything you didn’t ask for.
Dealer stickers above Toyota’s. Some dealers print their own price over Toyota’s: one buyer saw $2,838 added to a TRD Off-Road. Negotiate down from Toyota’s window sticker.
The model year. A 2026 and a 2027 look alike on the lot. In Chicago and Dallas, only the 2026 has offers.
The Toyota Financial Services requirement. The 3.99%, the leases and the $500 rebates need Toyota’s own financing. Compare the total cost with your bank’s rate.
Fees. Documentation fees in owner reports ran from $225 to $899, and one Florida dealer’s quotes carried $1,402 in fees in CarEdge’s data. Compare out-the-door prices.
Open recalls. On a 2024 or 2025, ask the dealer to show that every recall is done before you take delivery.
faq: Is the Toyota Tacoma a good truck?

Most reviewers think so. Kelley Blue Book rates the 2026 a 4.8 out of 5 and first among midsize trucks, U.S. News gives it 8.8 and second of seven, and J.D. Power’s owner score of 84 ranks it first among midsize pickups. Edmunds is cooler, at 6.8 and third of seven, and faults the cramped back seat and engine noise under hard acceleration. A Tacoma loses 19.5% of its value in five years by iSeeCars’ figures, against 30.2% for midsize pickups.
How much under MSRP can you get a Toyota Tacoma?

On a 2026 SR5, TRD PreRunner, TRD Sport or TRD Off-Road, 5–6% under MSRP is a fair deal and 7–8% is a strong one. The base SR and the hybrids have less room, around 2–4%, and the TRD Pro sells near sticker. Those ranges are our read of TrueCar’s averages, Edmunds’ suggested prices and CarWhere’s verified buyers, so a given dealer may land a point either side, and Toyota has no cash back to add on top.
Should I buy a 2026 or a 2027 Tacoma?

The 2026, for most buyers. It costs $180 to $520 less, and nearly all of Toyota’s offers are on the 2026: 3.99% financing, the SR5’s $500 finance cash and the leases. The 2027 gets 4.99% in Southern California and the New York area only. Toyota lists the same 11 trims for both years.
What is the destination charge on a Tacoma?
$1,745 on the 2026. Toyota’s advertised starting prices leave it out, so a $32,545 SR is $34,290 on the window sticker.
Does Toyota offer cash back on the Tacoma?

No. In Chicago, Dallas, Los Angeles and New York on November 16, 2026, Toyota offered financing from 2.99% and lease deals, but no customer cash. The only money off is $500 on a 2026 SR5 financed through Toyota in three of those regions, and a $500 military or college rebate when you finance or lease through Toyota Financial Services.
Is the Tacoma i-FORCE MAX hybrid worth it?

Only if you want its power or its 2,400-watt outlet. It makes 326 hp and 465 lb-ft against 278 hp and 317 lb-ft, but it costs $3,720 more on a TRD Sport 4x4 and is rated 23 mpg combined against 21. Edmunds timed a hybrid TRD Pro at 7.4 seconds to 60 mph against 7.6 for a gas TRD Sport.
Is a used Tacoma a better deal than new?

Rarely. CarWhere’s median asking price for a used 2024 is $38,119 and for a 2025 $38,635, while TrueCar’s average paid for a new 2026 SR5 starts at $36,274. Used loans averaged 11.19% in the second quarter of 2026, against Toyota’s 3.99% on a new one. A Gold Certified 2024 or 2025 with its recalls done is the used route we’d take.

vehicles.title: Toyota Corolla Price: MSRP, Discounts and What to Pay | Steer Me Right
vehicles.description: What a Toyota Corolla costs in November 2026: MSRP by trim for the 2026 and 2027 sedan, Hybrid and Hatchback, how far under sticker dealers sell it, Toyota’s current offers, and the GR Corolla.
vehicles.h1: Toyota Corolla price: what to pay and how far under MSRP to aim
vehicles.summary: The Corolla is the sensible small car most people expect: rated 50 mpg combined as a Hybrid LE, five stars overall from NHTSA, and it loses value slowly (9.3% in three years by iSeeCars’ count, against 24.8% for the average vehicle). It isn’t quick or roomy, though. Edmunds rates it 6.0 out of 10 and ninth of 10 compact sedans, faulting its 8.8-second run to 60 mph, highway noise and a 13.1-cubic-foot trunk. Unlike most Toyotas, it’s negotiable: TrueCar’s November averages put a gas LE about 7% under its sticker. Price a 2026 Hybrid LE, aim for 3–4% under MSRP, and take Toyota’s 4.99% financing if your bank can’t beat it. Prices and offers were checked on November 16, 2026.

after: The 2027s cost $200 more ($300 on the Hatchback XSE) with the same engines, and the 2027 Hatchback XSE gets the 10.5-inch screen and 12.3-inch gauges as standard. Toyota’s $1,295 destination charge is extra on every trim. The 2026 Hatchback FX Edition ($26,980 on Toyota’s November price list, 1,600 built) adds a rear wing, white 18-inch wheels and suede-trimmed heated seats, and a 60th Anniversary Hybrid SE (2,500 built) arrives in early 2027 with its price still to come.

pick: A 2026 Hybrid LE. At $24,975 it costs $1,850 more than a gas LE with the same equipment, and it’s rated 50 mpg combined against 35. Over 12,000 miles a year, that’s about 100 fewer gallons of gas. You keep the wireless CarPlay, blind-spot monitor and 7-inch digital gauges that every 2026 Corolla gets. AWD adds $1,400 and costs 2 mpg (48 combined), which only makes sense if you see snow.

Step up to the Hybrid XLE ($29,340) if you want heated SofTex seats, a moonroof and the 10.5-inch screen. Skip the Hybrid SE: its 18-inch wheels drop it to 47 mpg combined for $2,440 more than the LE. If you need a hatch, the Hatchback SE ($24,580) is gas-only and rated 35 mpg combined.

intro: Corollas are easier to discount than most Toyotas. Cox Automotive counted 36 days of supply at the end of October, tight next to the industry’s 87 but loose for a Toyota, whose RAV4s sat at 24. TrueCar’s November averages put the gas LE about 7% under its sticker with destination, the SE and Hybrid LE about 5–6%, and the XSE, Hybrid SE, Hybrid XLE and Hatchback about 2–3%. CarWhere’s 52 verified 2026 buyers paid a median 4.6% under MSRP.

intro: Our take: buy new, and buy the 2026. A used Corolla barely costs less than a discounted new one, used-loan rates average 11.19% against Toyota’s 4.99%, and the 2026 keeps two years or 25,000 miles of ToyotaCare maintenance, which the 2027 cuts to one year or 10,000 miles.

rows.when: Most buyers. It costs $200 less than the 2027 and keeps two years or 25,000 miles of ToyotaCare.
rows.check: That the car is a 2026 and not a 2027, and that Toyota’s offer runs in your region.

rows.when: You want the 2027 Hatchback XSE’s 10.5-inch screen and 12.3-inch gauges, or the 60th Anniversary Hybrid.
rows.check: The $200 to $300 price rise, and ToyotaCare cut to one year or 10,000 miles.

rows.when: You want a 2021 to 2025 with a warranty, and you’re paying cash.
rows.check: That it’s Gold Certified, not Silver. Gold adds a 12-month/12,000-mile comprehensive warranty and 7-year/100,000-mile powertrain coverage; Silver gives 12 months of powertrain cover only. A hybrid’s battery stays covered for 10 years/150,000 miles from first sale.

rows.when: Your budget is under about $20,000.
rows.check: Open recalls by VIN, an independent inspection, and on a 2019 or 2020, that the fuel pump and the stall software were done (Toyota covers that pump for 15 years).

after: If you buy used, skip the 2020. It drew 316 NHTSA owner complaints, more than any Corolla since, and needed a software fix for stalling at low speed as well as a fuel pump recall. A used 2025 asks a median $22,016 at about 34,000 miles in CarWhere’s November listings, while TrueCar shows buyers paying an average $22,665 for a new 2026 LE, destination included. Check any used Corolla’s open recalls by VIN: the 2023 and 2024 were recalled for a steering shaft that can crack, and the 2023 to 2025 Hybrid for brake assist that can drop out in turns (both free fixes).

watch: Dealer add-ons. Toyota dealers put add-ons on 37.7% of the quotes CarWhere studied, averaging $1,637. That’s a big share of a $25,000 car’s discount. Paint protection, nitrogen and etched VINs are the dealer’s products. Refuse or negotiate them.
The model year. A 2026 and a 2027 look alike on the lot. The 2027 costs $200 more, and its ToyotaCare covers one year or 10,000 miles against two years or 25,000.
The Toyota Financial Services requirement. The 4.99% and the $500 rebates need Toyota’s own financing. Compare the total cost with your bank’s rate.
Destination. Toyota’s $1,295 charge is the same at every dealer, except in AL, AR, FL, GA, LA, MS, NC, OK, SC and TX, where Toyota says it’s higher. Compare out-the-door prices.
The wrong hybrid. An AWD Hybrid SE is rated 44 mpg combined against 50 for a front-drive Hybrid LE. Check the window sticker if fuel economy is why you’re buying.
The headlight recall. NHTSA recall 26V110000 covers 2026 Corollas with incorrectly aimed headlights. Ask the dealer to show it’s done before you take delivery.
faq: Is the Toyota Corolla a good car?

Reviewers split. U.S. News scores it 8.6 out of 10 and named it a finalist for 2026 Best Compact Car for the Money, and KBB gives it 4.5 out of 5. Edmunds rates it 6.0 and ninth of 10 compact sedans, and Car and Driver (7.5 out of 10) prefers the Civic and Mazda 3. Consumer Reports expects it to be more reliable than the average new car, and a three-year-old Corolla has lost 9.3% of its value by iSeeCars’ figures, against 24.8% for the average vehicle.
How much under MSRP can you get a Toyota Corolla?

On a 2026 gas LE or SE, 5–6% under MSRP is a fair deal and 7% or more is a strong one. Hybrids sell closer to sticker, so 3–4% is fair, and the XSE and Hatchback about 2–3%. Those ranges are our read of TrueCar’s November averages and CarWhere’s verified buyers (a median 4.6% under), so a given dealer may land a point either side. Toyota has no cash back to add on top.
Should I buy a 2026 or a 2027 Corolla?

The 2026, for most buyers. It costs $200 less with the same engines, and it keeps two years or 25,000 miles of ToyotaCare maintenance, which Toyota cut to one year or 10,000 miles for the 2027. Wait for the 2027 if you want the Hatchback XSE’s bigger screens or the 60th Anniversary Hybrid (2,500 built, due early 2027).
Is the Corolla Hybrid worth it?

For most buyers, yes. A Hybrid LE costs $1,850 more than a gas LE and is rated 50 mpg combined against 35, about 100 fewer gallons a year at 12,000 miles. Edmunds tells shoppers to look at the hybrid first. Toyota covers the hybrid battery for 10 years or 150,000 miles and the other hybrid parts for 8 years or 100,000.
What is the destination charge on a Corolla?

$1,295 on the 2026 and the 2027, sedan, Hybrid, Hatchback or GR Corolla. It was $1,195 when the 2026 launched. Toyota’s advertised starting prices leave it out, and Toyota says it’s higher in AL, AR, FL, GA, LA, MS, NC, OK, SC and TX.
Does Toyota offer cash back on the Corolla?

No. In Chicago, Dallas, Los Angeles and New York on November 16, 2026, Toyota offered 4.99% financing for 48 months and lease deals, but no customer cash. The only money off is a $500 military or college rebate when you finance or lease through Toyota Financial Services.
How much is a GR Corolla?

The 2026 starts at $40,520 with the manual and $42,520 with the automatic; the Premium Plus is $46,565 and $48,565, all before the $1,295 destination charge. Dealers no longer mark it up: Edmunds found it selling about $1,500 under sticker in November. The two-seat GRMN Corolla is $64,360, with 730 built worldwide.
Is a used Corolla a better deal than new?

Rarely. CarWhere’s median asking price for a used 2025 is $22,016 at about 34,000 miles, and TrueCar’s average paid for a new 2026 LE is $22,665 with destination. Used loans averaged 11.19% in the second quarter of 2026, against Toyota’s 4.99% on a new one. A Gold Certified 2021 to 2025 is the used route we’d take.

spotlight.heading: GR Corolla: the 300-hp one
intro: The GR Corolla shares the hatchback’s body and little else: a 300-hp turbocharged 1.6-liter three-cylinder, all-wheel drive that can send up to 70% of the power to the rear, and Torsen limited-slip differentials front and rear. Car and Driver gives the 2026 a 9.5 out of 10 and an Editors’ Choice; Edmunds rates it 6.9 and fourth of five hot hatches, marking it down for a plain Corolla cabin, highway noise and the smallest cargo area of its rivals (17.8 cubic feet).

intro: You no longer pay over sticker for one. Edmunds counted about 1,900 new GR Corollas in stock nationwide in November, selling about $1,500 under sticker, and its Texas price data puts both trims about $2,000 under MSRP with destination. iSeeCars puts dealer invoice about 6% under MSRP.

rows.why: Edmunds’ Texas prices run about 5% under. There’s no cash back from Toyota.

after: Buy the base GR Corolla with the manual. It’s the cheapest version ($40,520) and the quickest: Car and Driver’s manual car reached 60 mph in 4.2 seconds against 5.0 for its automatic, and the manual is rated 24 mpg combined against 22. Premium Plus adds $6,045 of comfort (heated seats and steering wheel, JBL audio, a head-up display) and an extra radiator; Edmunds suggests it only if you’ll do regular track days. The $64,360 GRMN Corolla is a two-seat, 730-car collector’s edition, so price it separately.

A used one barely saves money. CarWhere’s median 2024 asks $36,997 at about 22,500 miles, $3,500 under a new base manual that comes with a full warranty. Owners of 2023 and 2024 manuals filed NHTSA complaints about clutches wearing out early, and Car and Driver says the 2026 clutch is better suited to hard use, so have any used manual’s clutch checked. Toyota warns that track driving can cause damage its warranty won’t cover.

vehicles.h1: Honda Civic price: what to pay and how far under MSRP to aim
vehicles.summary: The Civic is the compact car to beat, and the hybrid is why: U.S. News ranks the Civic first among compact cars and Edmunds ranks the Civic Hybrid first among compact sedans. A 2026 Sport Hybrid is rated 49 mpg combined and reached 60 mph in 6.6 seconds in Edmunds’ test, where a gas Civic Sport took 10.0, and it holds its value better than almost anything: iSeeCars counts 7.0% lost in three years, against 24.8% for the average vehicle. The catch is price. It starts above a Corolla or Elantra, and dealers give less off: Edmunds’ Texas prices run about 1–2% under sticker, and CarWhere’s verified buyers paid a median 4.5% under. Price a 2026 Sport Hybrid, aim for 1–2% under MSRP, and take Honda’s 3.99% financing before it ends November 30. Prices and offers were checked on November 16, 2026.

after: Every 2027 that carries over costs $300 more, and Honda’s $1,295 destination charge is extra on both years. The 2027 adds the gas Sport-L and gives the Sport Touring Hybrid Honda’s S+ Shift drive mode, and the 2027 hybrid hatchback is rated 47 mpg combined against 48. Honda has no 2027 Si, so the 2026 is the last one for now. The Type R ($47,395 for 2026, $48,695 for 2027) has its own section below.

pick: A 2026 Sport Hybrid sedan. At $29,395 it costs $2,700 more than a gas Sport, and it’s rated 49 mpg combined against 34. Over 12,000 miles a year, that’s about 110 fewer gallons of gas. It’s quicker too: 200 hp against 150, and 6.6 seconds to 60 mph in Edmunds’ test against 10.0 for a gas Sport. It adds heated front seats, a moonroof and dual-zone climate control, and it’s Edmunds’ pick of the line. Honda’s 3.99% financing covers it as a 2026.

Step up to the Sport Touring Hybrid ($32,395) for leather, wireless CarPlay, Google built-in and Bose audio. Skip the LX unless price is everything: it’s $4,700 less but has a 7-inch screen with wired CarPlay and no heated seats. Need room for gear? The Hatchback Sport Hybrid ($30,595) has 24.5 cubic feet of cargo space against the sedan’s 14.8-cubic-foot trunk.

intro: Civics sell closer to sticker than Corollas. Honda dealers had 57 days of supply at the end of October by Cox Automotive’s count (it doesn’t list the Civic on its own), yet Edmunds’ Texas prices put a 2026 LX only about 2% under its sticker with destination and a Sport Hybrid about 1%. CarWhere’s 68 verified 2026 buyers did better, a median 4.5% under MSRP, and iSeeCars puts dealer invoice 4–5% under MSRP.

rows.why: Edmunds’ Texas price for an LX runs about 2% under. Invoice sits 4.2% under MSRP.
Edmunds’ Texas price for a Sport Hybrid runs about 1% under. Hybrids are over 30% of Civic sales.

intro: Our take: buy new, and buy the 2026. It costs $300 less than the 2027, Honda’s 3.99% financing covers only the 2026, and a used Civic barely costs less than a new one: CarWhere’s median used 2025 asks $25,575 at about 29,500 miles, while Edmunds’ Texas price for a new 2026 LX is $25,508 with destination.

after: If you buy used, look at a 2023 to 2025 and ask for proof that steering recall 24V744 is done. The 2022, the first year of this generation, drew 963 NHTSA owner complaints, 806 of them about steering, more than the 2023, 2024 and 2025 combined (592); 24V744 fixes a steering gearbox that can make the car hard to steer on 2022 to 2025 Civics, and it’s free. CarWhere’s 2023 figure isn’t shown because it had too few listings.

watch: Dealer add-ons. Honda dealers put add-ons on 35.1% of the quotes CarWhere studied, averaging $1,159. On a car that sells 1–2% under sticker, that can be more than the whole discount. Refuse or negotiate them.
The November 30 deadline. Honda’s 3.99% financing and the 2026 leases end November 30. The 2027 gets leases through January 4 but no special rate.
The model year. A 2026 and a 2027 look the same on the lot. The 2027 costs $300 more and Honda’s rate doesn’t cover it.
The Honda Financial Services requirement. The 3.99% and every $500 offer need Honda’s own financing. Compare the total cost with your bank’s rate.
“No payments for 90 days.” Interest still builds during those 90 days, so it isn’t a discount.
Steering on a used one. On a 2022 to 2025 Civic, ask for proof that steering recall 24V744 is done.
faq: Is the Honda Civic a good car?

Most reviewers rank it at or near the top of its class. U.S. News scores the 2026 a 9.4 out of 10 and first of eight compact cars, and Kelley Blue Book gives it 4.7 out of 5. Edmunds rates the gas Civic 6.9, marking it down for a slow base engine and highway noise, but rates the hybrid 7.9 and named it its 2026 Top Rated Car. J.D. Power owners give it 83 out of 100, and a three-year-old Civic has lost 7.0% of its value by iSeeCars’ figures, against 24.8% for the average vehicle.
How much under MSRP can you get a Honda Civic?

Less than on most compact cars. On a 2026 LX or Sport, 2–3% under MSRP is a fair deal and 4–5% a strong one. The hybrids sell closest to sticker, so 1–2% is fair and 3–4% strong. Those ranges are our read of Edmunds’ Texas prices (about 1–2% under), CarWhere’s 68 verified buyers (a median 4.5% under) and iSeeCars’ invoice figures, so a given dealer may land a point either side. Honda has no cash back to add on top.
Should I buy a 2026 or a 2027 Civic?

The 2026, for most buyers. It costs $300 less with the same engines, and Honda’s 3.99% financing covers only the 2026, through November 30. Buy the 2027 if you want the new gas Sport-L, with leather and heated seats, or S+ Shift on the Sport Touring Hybrid.
Is the Civic Hybrid worth it?

Yes, for most buyers. A Sport Hybrid sedan costs $2,700 more than a gas Sport and is rated 49 mpg combined against 34, about 110 fewer gallons a year at 12,000 miles. It’s also much quicker (6.6 seconds to 60 mph in Edmunds’ test against 10.0) and adds heated seats, a moonroof and dual-zone climate control. Honda says hybrids are now more than 30% of Civic sales.
What is the destination charge on a Civic?
$1,295 on the 2026 and the 2027, for every Civic including the Si and Type R. Honda’s advertised starting prices leave it out; the $455 premium paint charge is extra too.
Does Honda offer cash back on the Civic?

No. In Chicago, Dallas, Los Angeles and New York on November 16, 2026, Honda offered 3.99% financing on the 2026 and leases on both years, but no customer cash. The money off is a $500 loyalty offer for Honda owners on the sedans and a $500 military or graduate offer on every Civic, all through Honda Financial Services.
Is Honda still making the Civic Si?
Not for 2027. Honda lists no 2027 Si, so the 2026 ($31,495 plus $1,295 destination, six-speed manual only) is the last one for now. It has no special financing or lease from Honda.
How much is a Civic Type R?

The 2026 is $47,395 and the 2027 $48,695, both before the $1,295 destination charge. Markups have mostly gone: Kelley Blue Book’s fair purchase price for a 2026 is $48,100, a little under the $48,690 sticker with destination, and owners on the CivicXI forum report paying MSRP or a little under in 2026.
Is a used Civic a better deal than new?

Rarely. CarWhere’s median asking price for a used 2025 is $25,575 at about 29,500 miles, while Edmunds’ Texas price for a new 2026 LX is $25,508 with destination. Used loans averaged 11.19% in the second quarter of 2026, against Honda’s 3.99% on a new 2026. A HondaTrue Certified 2023 to 2025 is the used route we’d take.

spotlight.heading: Civic Type R: the 315-hp one
intro: The Type R shares the hatchback’s body with a 315-hp turbocharged 2.0-liter four, a six-speed manual (there’s no automatic) and a helical limited-slip differential driving the front wheels. Honda calls it America’s best-selling hot hatch. It keeps the hatchback’s 24.5 cubic feet of cargo space, against 17.8 in a GR Corolla. The 2027, at dealers since October, adds heated front seats, retuned dampers in +R mode, Google built-in and a reshaped front for $1,300 more.

vehicles.summary: A used Model Y is one of the easier EVs to buy at a dealer, as long as you pick the year with care. A 2023 averaged $33,200 in dealer listings in September, against $41,630 for the cheapest new Model Y with fees, and whatever is left of its 8-year battery warranty passes to you whoever sells it. The catch is how fast they sell: 16 days at the median, so dealers rarely need to cut much, and Tesla’s own used warranty covers only cars Tesla sells. Shop a 2024 Long Range, aim for 1–2% under asking, and make sure every recall is closed. Prices were checked on November 16, 2026.

intro: Used Model Ys don’t sit. Recurrent puts the median at 16 days from listing to sale between June and September, and Cox Automotive counted 35 days’ supply of used EVs in September against 46 for gas cars. Asking prices on 2024 and 2025 cars slipped 2.5–3.3% over the summer, while 2020s rose 2.9% as buyers chased the cheapest ones. Nobody publishes what used Model Ys sell for against their asking price, so the ranges below are our estimate from those figures.

after: Each 10,000 miles takes about $1,000 off a Model Y of the same year, Recurrent finds, so adjust for mileage before comparing two listings. The redesigned 2026, with its light-bar nose and quieter cabin, is still scarce used, and Tesla sells it new from $39,990 before fees.

pick: A 2024 Long Range, with AWD if you see snow. At an average asking price of $36,500 in September, it costs about $3,300 more than a 2023 and gets you three things: Hardware 4, since 2024s were built after the mid-2023 switch (the 2023s are a mix), five recall campaigns against 17 for the 2023, and battery and drive-unit cover that runs into 2032 or to 120,000 miles. The Long Range RWD is EPA-rated at 320 miles against 310 for the AWD.

On a tighter budget, a 2022 or 2023 Long Range AWD at $30,000 to $33,000 is the next step down; check the Autopilot computer and that the suspension, seat and steering recalls are closed. We’d skip a 2020 or 2021 unless the price allows for it: they carry the most recalls, their battery cover ends in 2028 or 2029, and the 2021 is the year NHTSA’s door handle investigation covers. The Performance gives up about 25 miles of EPA range to a Long Range of the same year.

intro: Our take: buy used, a 2023 or 2024, from whichever seller has the right car at the right price. A Model Y has taken its steepest drop by year three (44.1% by iSeeCars’ count, against 24.8% for the average car), so the second owner gets the bargain. Your credit decides how much of it you keep.

rows.when: You want to negotiate, or the car with the right year, range and miles is at a franchise or independent dealer.

after: Battery wear worries buyers more than the figures suggest. Aviloo’s tests put the median Model Y battery at 90% of its health at about 93,000 miles, and Tesla says Long Range packs lose about 15% after 200,000 miles. Battery and drive-unit cover passes to you from any seller: 8 years or 120,000 miles on a Long Range or Performance, as long as capacity stays above 70%.

rivals: Price a used Hyundai Ioniq 5 before you settle. Edmunds ranks the 2026 a step ahead of the Model Y (8.3 to 8.2), KBB’s experts give the 2023 a 4.7 against the Model Y’s 4.1, and a 2023 SEL’s Fair Purchase Price is $25,800 against $33,500 for a 2023 Model Y Long Range. The Ford Mustang Mach-E ($29,300 for a 2023 Premium) and Kia EV6 ($24,500 for a 2023 Wind) cost less too, and a Volkswagen ID.4 is the cheapest of the group. If you don’t need the Model Y’s hatch and height, a 2023 Model 3 Long Range runs about $3,400 less. Torn between two or three? Steer Me Right Pro prices up to three models side by side and gives you our pick.
watch: Open recalls. Run the VIN at NHTSA. The headlight recall on 2020–2023 cars (26V507) has no fix yet, and the suspension, seat belt, seat and steering wheel recalls on 2020–2023 cars need a service visit, not a software update.

The front suspension. NHTSA opened an investigation in July 2026 into front lateral links failing on 2021–2023 Model Ys, many with no warning. Have an independent shop look at the front suspension before you buy.

Hardware 3 or 4. Most cars built before mid-2023 have Hardware 3, which Tesla says can’t run unsupervised FSD. Look under Settings, Software, Additional Vehicle Information for the Autopilot computer.

FSD in the listing. Tesla now sells FSD only as a subscription, and says FSD bought outright stays with the car. If a listing charges extra for it, check that it shows on the car’s screen before you pay.

The “warranty” on the window. A dealer’s warranty on a used Model Y is its own or a third party’s. Tesla’s used warranty covers only cars Tesla sells. Ask for the first delivery date to see how much battery cover is left.

Door handles on a 2021. NHTSA is investigating 2021 Model Ys whose outside handles stop working when the 12-volt battery runs low. Ask when the 12-volt battery was last replaced, and learn where the manual door releases are.
Add-ons and fees. Used-car dealers add paint protection, etching and service contracts. Compare out-the-door prices, and refuse what you didn’t ask for.
faq: How much is a used Tesla Model Y?

Dealers listed them at an average of $26,400 for a 2020 up to $39,700 for a 2025 in September 2026, by Recurrent’s count. Each 10,000 miles takes about $1,000 off a car of the same year. A new Model Y starts at $39,990 before $1,640 in fees.
How much under asking can you get a used Model Y?

On a 2023 to 2025, 1–2% under asking is a fair deal and 3–4% a strong one; on a 2020 to 2022, about 1% is fair and 2–3% strong. Those ranges are our estimate: used Model Ys sell in about 16 days, so dealers rarely need to cut much, and Tesla doesn’t negotiate on its own used cars.
What is the best year for a used Model Y?

The 2024, in our view. It was built after the switch to Hardware 4, has five recall campaigns against 17 to 24 for the 2020 to 2023, and battery cover that runs into 2032. A 2023 built after mid-year is the next best, at about $3,300 less.
Does the Tesla battery warranty transfer to a used buyer?

Yes, at no cost, whoever sells you the car. It runs 8 years or 120,000 miles on a Long Range or Performance and 8 years or 100,000 miles on a Standard or Standard Range, counted from first delivery, and covers capacity that falls below 70%.
Does a used Model Y from a dealer come with Tesla’s warranty?

Not Tesla’s used warranty. Its 1-year/10,000-mile cover applies only to used cars Tesla sells and delivers itself. The remainder of the original 4-year/50,000-mile basic warranty and the battery warranty do carry over.
Does Full Self-Driving transfer with a used Model Y?

Tesla says FSD bought outright stays with the car, and it now sells FSD only as a subscription, which doesn’t carry over. Check that FSD shows on the car’s own screen before you pay extra for it, and check for Hardware 4: Tesla says Hardware 3 cars can’t run unsupervised FSD.
Is a used Model Y reliable?

Mixed. U.S. News predicts 78 out of 100 for the 2026. Owners of three-year-old Teslas reported 226 problems per 100 vehicles in J.D. Power’s 2026 dependability study, against an industry average of 204, and Germany’s TÜV failed 17.3% of two- to three-year-old Model Ys at inspection, mostly for suspension parts, brake discs and lights.

vehicles.summary: The Camry is the midsize sedan most buyers should start with, and since 2025 every one is a hybrid: a front-drive LE is rated 51 mpg combined, U.S. News ranks it first of nine hybrid cars, and IIHS names it a 2026 Top Safety Pick+, a grade above the Honda Accord’s Top Safety Pick. It holds its value, too, losing 22% in three years by iSeeCars’ count against 24.8% for the average vehicle. The catches: Edmunds and U.S. News both find the engine coarse when you push it, and Edmunds rates the 15.1-cubic-foot trunk smaller on paper than the Accord’s or Hyundai Sonata’s. It’s also easier to discount than its tight supply suggests: Edmunds’ Texas prices run about 7–8% under sticker, and CarWhere’s 90 verified buyers paid a median 6.2% under MSRP. Price a 2026 XLE, aim for 4–5% under MSRP, and take Toyota’s 4.99% financing if your bank can’t beat it. Prices and offers were checked on November 17, 2026.

after: AWD adds $1,525 on every 2026 trim, and Toyota’s $1,295 destination charge is extra on both years. The 2027 costs $100 more with the same engines and equipment, but its ToyotaCare maintenance covers one year or 10,000 miles against two years or 25,000 on the 2026. Toyota has raised the Camry’s price since the 2025 launch (a 2025 LE was $28,700), so some review sites still print lower 2026 figures; these are toyota.com’s.

pick: A 2026 XLE. At $34,800 it costs $2,700 more than an SE, and the step up buys a 12.3-inch touchscreen and 12.3-inch digital gauges in place of an 8-inch screen and 7-inch gauges, heated leather-and-microfiber front seats, a power passenger seat and acoustic glass in the front doors. It’s rated 46 mpg combined, the same as an SE, and it’s Edmunds’ pick of the line. AWD adds $1,525 and costs nothing in the EPA’s figures on the XLE (46 mpg combined either way), so take it if you see snow.

Pick the LE ($29,600) if price and mileage come first: it’s rated 51 mpg combined, about 25 fewer gallons a year than an XLE at 12,000 miles, but it has cloth seats and an 8-inch screen. Skip the XSE with AWD: its 19-inch wheels drop it to 43 mpg combined for $1,200 more than an AWD XLE.

intro: Camrys sell under sticker even though they’re scarce. Cox Automotive counted 28 days of supply at the end of October, against 39 for Toyota and 87 for the industry, and Edmunds says new Camrys sell in a median 10 days. Kelley Blue Book’s fair purchase price, only $295 to $395 under MSRP, is far less generous.

intro: Our take: buy new, and buy the 2026. A used Camry barely costs less than a discounted new one: CarWhere’s median used 2025 asks $27,989 at about 40,000 miles, while Edmunds’ Texas price for a new 2026 LE is $28,450 with destination. Used loans average 11.19% against Toyota’s 4.99%, and the 2026 keeps two years or 25,000 miles of ToyotaCare, which the 2027 cuts to one year or 10,000 miles.

rows.when: Most buyers. It costs $100 less than the 2027 and keeps two years or 25,000 miles of ToyotaCare.
rows.check: That the car is a 2026, that Toyota’s rate covers the 2026 in your region, and that inverter recall 25V869 is done if the car is on it.

rows.when: Toyota’s rate covers only the 2027 where you live (the Midwest, when we checked), or the color you want is only on a 2027.
rows.check: The $100 price rise, and ToyotaCare cut to one year or 10,000 miles.

rows.check: That it’s Gold Certified, not Silver. Gold adds a 12-month/12,000-mile comprehensive warranty and 7-year/100,000-mile powertrain coverage; Silver gives 12 months of powertrain cover only. A 2025’s hybrid battery stays covered for 10 years/150,000 miles from first sale.

after: If you buy used, look at a 2022 to 2024 gas Camry or a 2025 hybrid, and skip the 2019 and 2020. Those two drew 417 and 287 NHTSA owner complaints, more than any Camry since, and their fuel pumps were recalled. The 2022 to 2024 drew 53 to 69 a year. The 2025, the first hybrid-only Camry, drew 179, about 27 of them describing a front bumper cover that comes loose and 21 a cracked windshield, and it has six recalls, including 25V869 (an inverter bolt that can cut power or cause a fire; Toyota replaces the inverter free). Check any used Camry’s open recalls by VIN.

watch: Dealer add-ons. Toyota dealers put add-ons on 37.7% of the quotes CarWhere studied, averaging $1,637. On a $36,000 XLE, that’s most of a fair discount. Paint protection, nitrogen and etched VINs are the dealer’s products. Refuse or negotiate them.
The model year. A 2026 and a 2027 look alike on the lot. The 2027 costs $100 more, and its ToyotaCare covers one year or 10,000 miles against two years or 25,000.

The inverter recall. NHTSA recall 25V869 covers some 2025 and 2026 Camrys with an inverter bolt that may not be tight, which can cut power or cause a fire. Ask the dealer to show the inverter was replaced before you take delivery.
The Toyota Financial Services requirement. The 4.99% and the college rebate need Toyota’s own financing. Compare the total cost with your bank’s rate.
The wrong wheels. An AWD XSE is rated 43 mpg combined against 46 for an AWD XLE and 50 for an AWD LE. Check the window sticker if fuel economy is why you’re buying.
Which year the rate covers. Toyota’s 4.99% was on the 2027 only in Chicago and on the 2026 only in Los Angeles. Ask which model year the dealer’s quote assumes.
faq: Is the Toyota Camry a good car?

Most reviewers rank it at or near the top of its class. U.S. News scores the 2026 a 9.4 out of 10, first of nine hybrid cars, and named it the 2026 Best Midsize Hybrid Car for the Money. Edmunds rates it 8.4, Kelley Blue Book 4.8 out of 5 with its Best Buy Award, and J.D. Power owners 82 out of 100. Consumer Reports expects it to be more reliable than the average new car, and iSeeCars counts 22% of its value lost in three years, against 24.8% for the average vehicle.
How much under MSRP can you get a Toyota Camry?

More than on most Toyotas. On a 2026 LE, SE or XSE, 5–6% under MSRP is a fair deal and 7% or more a strong one; the Nightshade and XLE are harder to find, so 4–5% is fair. Those ranges are our read of Edmunds’ Texas prices (about 7–8% under sticker), CarWhere’s 90 verified buyers (a median 6.2% under) and iSeeCars’ invoice figures, so a given dealer may land a point either side. Toyota has no cash back to add on top.
Should I buy a 2026 or a 2027 Camry?

The 2026, for most buyers. It costs $100 less with the same engine and equipment, and it keeps two years or 25,000 miles of ToyotaCare maintenance, which Toyota cut to one year or 10,000 miles for the 2027. Buy the 2027 if Toyota’s 4.99% covers only the 2027 in your region, as it did in Chicago.
Is every Camry a hybrid?

Yes, since the 2025 redesign. Every Camry has a 2.5-liter four-cylinder hybrid with 225 hp, or 232 hp with AWD. The EPA rates the front-drive LE at 51 mpg combined and the other front-drive trims at 46. Toyota covers the hybrid battery for 10 years or 150,000 miles and the other hybrid parts for 8 years or 100,000.
Is AWD worth it on a Camry?

If you see snow, yes. It adds $1,525 on every trim and costs little in fuel: the EPA rates an AWD SE or XLE at 46 mpg combined, the same as front drive, and an AWD LE at 50 against 51. The AWD XSE drops to 43 because of its 19-inch wheels.
What is the destination charge on a Camry?
$1,295 on the 2026, up from $1,195 on the 2025. Toyota’s advertised starting prices leave it out.
Does Toyota offer cash back on the Camry?

No. In Chicago, Dallas, Los Angeles and New York on November 17, 2026, Toyota offered 4.99% financing for 48 months and lease deals, but no customer cash. The only money off is a $500 military or college rebate.
Is a used Camry a better deal than new?

Rarely. CarWhere’s median asking price for a used 2025 is $27,989 at about 40,000 miles, and Edmunds’ Texas price for a new 2026 LE is $28,450 with destination. Used loans averaged 11.19% in the second quarter of 2026, against Toyota’s 4.99% on a new one. A Gold Certified 2022 to 2025 is the used route we’d take.

vehicles.h1: Honda Accord price: what to pay and how far under MSRP to aim
vehicles.summary: The Accord is the midsize sedan most reviewers would buy, and the hybrid is the version to get: U.S. News ranks the Accord first of four midsize cars, though Edmunds puts the hybrid-only Toyota Camry a place ahead. An EX-L Hybrid is rated 48 mpg combined against 31 for a gas SE, and a three-year-old Accord has lost 15.5% of its value by iSeeCars’ count, against 24.8% for the average vehicle. The catches are no all-wheel drive and no blind-spot warning on the base LX. Dealers give more room than on a Civic: TrueCar’s November averages run 1.2% to 4.9% under sticker by trim, and Edmunds’ Texas prices 2.3% to 5.7%. Price a 2026 EX-L Hybrid, aim for 3–4% under MSRP, and weigh Honda’s 3.49–3.99% financing against your bank’s before it ends January 4. Prices and offers were checked on November 17, 2026.

after: Honda’s $1,295 destination charge is extra on every trim. It was $1,195 until Honda’s September 9, 2026 price list, so some sites, Kelley Blue Book among them, still print a $29,590 starting price with destination; the trim prices themselves haven’t changed since launch. Every Accord is front-wheel drive. The LX is rated 32 mpg combined and the SE 31; the EX-L Hybrid is rated 48 on its 17-inch wheels and the other hybrids 44 on 19s. Honda hasn’t announced a U.S. 2027 Accord.

pick: A 2026 EX-L Hybrid. At $35,095 it costs $1,300 more than the Sport Hybrid and adds leather, a power passenger seat, driver’s seat memory and parking sensors. Its 17-inch wheels also lift it to 48 mpg combined against 44 for the other hybrids, and Edmunds expects them to ride better than the 19s it tested. Against a gas SE it’s $4,400 more and rated 48 mpg against 31: over 12,000 miles a year, that’s about 135 fewer gallons. Edmunds timed a Sport-L Hybrid at 7.0 seconds to 60 mph; U.S. News took 8.5 seconds in a gas SE.

Step up to the Touring Hybrid ($39,495) for Bose audio, ventilated front seats, heated rear seats, a head-up display and Google built-in; it also sells furthest under sticker. Skip the LX unless price is everything: it’s $2,300 less than the SE but has no heated seats, no moonroof and no blind-spot warning.

TrueCar’s November averages, from 513 sales, put the 2026 at 1.2% to 4.9% under sticker by trim; Edmunds’ Texas prices run 2.3% to 5.7% under, and CarWhere’s 105 verified buyers of 2025 and 2026 Accords paid a median 6.3% under MSRP.
