A scarce EX-L. Edmunds says EX-L Hybrid stock is much tighter than the other trims’. If none is near you, the Sport-L Hybrid has the same leather and power seats for $400 more; don’t pay over sticker for an EX-L.
The Honda Financial Services requirement. The low rates and the $500 offers need Honda’s own financing. Compare the total cost with your bank’s rate.
“No payments for 90 days.” Interest still builds during those 90 days, so it isn’t a discount.
Recalls on a used one. On a 2023 or 2024, ask for proof that fuel pump recall 24V763 is done; on a 2023 to 2025 Hybrid, software recall 25V785, which fixes a fault that can cut drive power.
faq: Is the Honda Accord a good car?

Most reviewers rank it at or near the top of its class. U.S. News scores the 2026 a 9.5 out of 10 and first of four midsize cars, and Kelley Blue Book gives it 4.8 out of 5. Edmunds rates it 8.3, second of six midsize sedans behind the Toyota Camry. J.D. Power owners give it 82 out of 100, Consumer Reports expects it to be more reliable than the average new car, and NHTSA gives it five stars in every test.
How much under MSRP can you get a Honda Accord?

More than on most Hondas. On an LX, SE or Sport Hybrid, 2–3% under MSRP is a fair deal and 4–5% a strong one; on an EX-L or Sport-L Hybrid, 3–4% is fair and 5–6% strong; on a Touring Hybrid, 4–5% is fair and 6% or more strong. Those ranges are our read of TrueCar’s November averages (1.2–4.9% under by trim), Edmunds’ Texas prices (2.3–5.7%) and CarWhere’s 105 verified buyers (a median 6.3% under), so a given dealer may land a point either side. Honda has no cash back to add on top.
Is the Accord Hybrid worth it?

Yes, for most buyers. An EX-L Hybrid costs $4,400 more than a gas SE and is rated 48 mpg combined against 31, about 135 fewer gallons a year at 12,000 miles. It adds leather and more power (204 hp against 192), and Honda says hybrids were more than half of Accord sales in 2025. The hybrid does lose value a little faster: 22.1% in three years by iSeeCars’ count, against 15.5% for the Accord overall.
Is there a 2027 Honda Accord?

Not in the U.S. yet. On November 17, 2026, Honda’s site and press releases listed only the 2026, and Honda hadn’t announced a 2027 price; Edmunds lists a 2027 as upcoming. The 2026 is the one to price now.
What is the destination charge on an Accord?

$1,295 on every 2026 Accord, from Honda’s September 9, 2026 price list. It was $1,195 when the 2026 launched, which is why some sites still show a $29,590 starting price; with today’s charge an LX is $29,690.
Does Honda offer cash back on the Accord?

No. In Chicago, Dallas, Los Angeles and New York on November 17, 2026, Honda offered 3.49–3.99% financing and leases on the 2026 but no customer cash. The money off is $750 for Honda owners and $500 for military buyers and recent graduates, the last through Honda Financial Services.
Should I buy an Accord or a Toyota Camry?

Price both. The Camry is hybrid-only, starts at $29,600, $4,195 less than the cheapest Accord Hybrid, offers all-wheel drive and is an IIHS Top Safety Pick+, and Edmunds rates it the better car. The Accord has the bigger discounts and a gas version from $28,395. See our Camry price guide.
Is a used Accord a better deal than new?

Rarely. CarWhere’s median asking price for a used 2025 is $28,124 at about 17,700 miles, while Edmunds’ Texas price for a new 2026 LX is $29,018 with destination. Used loans averaged 11.19% in the second quarter of 2026, against Honda’s 3.99% on a new one. A HondaTrue Certified 2023 to 2025 is the used route we’d take.

vehicles.title: Toyota Tundra Price: MSRP, Discounts and What to Pay | Steer Me Right
vehicles.description: What a Toyota Tundra costs in November 2026: MSRP by trim for 2026 and 2027, how far under sticker dealers sell it, Toyota’s current offers, and whether to buy new, used or CPO.
vehicles.h1: Toyota Tundra price: what to pay and how far under MSRP to aim
vehicles.summary: The Tundra is the full-size pickup for buyers who want a smooth twin-turbo V6, a roomy cab and strong resale, and who don’t need the biggest tow rating. Kelley Blue Book named it the 2026 best-resale full-size pickup, and iSeeCars puts its five-year depreciation at 19.7% against 37.0% for the class. It isn’t the strongest tower or hauler (Toyota lists up to 12,000 pounds and 1,850 pounds of payload), and Edmunds ranks it fourth of five large trucks and measured 15.2 mpg on its test route. It does sell under sticker: TrueCar’s trim averages run 3–7% under, Edmunds’ Texas suggested prices 7–10% under, and CarWhere’s 27 verified buyers paid a median 7.5% under MSRP. Price a 2026 Limited, aim for 5–7% under MSRP, and take Toyota’s 1.99% to 2.99% financing if your bank can’t beat it. Prices and offers were checked on November 18, 2026.

after: Prices leave out the $2,195 destination charge. 4x4 adds $3,000 on every gas trim we checked (iSeeCars’ list), and the i-FORCE MAX adds $3,700 to a Limited. The Platinum, 1794 Edition, TRD Pro and Capstone hybrids start as 4x4s. For 2027 every trim goes up $640 to $2,835, except the i-FORCE MAX Limited: its $63,090 is $4,530 over the 2026 starting price, and Toyota’s page doesn’t say which drive that price is for. Toyota lists the same 10 trims for 2027 and a Trailhunter package it hasn’t priced.

pick: A 2026 Limited CrewMax, with 4x4 if you tow or leave pavement. At $54,860 it adds a 14-inch touchscreen, 20-inch wheels and heated and ventilated leather seats to the SR5, and Edmunds’ editors pick it for the lineup too. It’s also the cheapest way into the hybrid, and TrueCar’s averages show it selling 6.4% under sticker, more than any other gas trim. 4x4 adds $3,000. The SR5 is $8,350 less, has the same V6, the tow hitch and the trailer brake controller, and has the most stock (Edmunds), so it’s the one to price if the leather and the big screen don’t matter to you.

Skip the i-FORCE MAX hybrid unless you want its torque (583 lb-ft against 479). It adds $3,700 to a Limited and is rated 20 mpg combined against 19 in 4x4 (22 against 20 in 2WD), and Edmunds calls the setup more about power than efficiency. Toyota’s 1.99% reaches the hybrids in all four regions we checked but the gas Limited only in Dallas, which narrows the gap if you finance. The TRD Pro starts at $72,565, sells near sticker and gets none of Toyota’s cash or rate offers.

intro: Tundras sell quickly but not at sticker. Edmunds counts about 28,600 new ones nationwide, selling in about 30 days against 34 for the average new vehicle, and Toyota had 39 days of supply at the end of October against 87 for the industry. Buyers still get real money off: CarWhere’s 27 verified 2026 buyers paid a median 7.5% under MSRP, Edmunds’ suggested prices, based on Texas sales, run 7–10% under, and TrueCar’s trim averages run 3–7% under. Dealer invoice is about 7.5% under MSRP before destination. The TRD Pro has the least room.

choice.text: Each bar is how much less you pay in total than at the 6.35% average new-car rate, on a $57,000 Tundra over 72 months. The cash and the rate don’t combine, and the rate wins by a wide margin: even a buyer who finances after the $1,000 cash at the 4.41% that borrowers with top credit averaged comes out about $3,350 behind the 1.99%. Get your bank’s rate before you sign.

intro: Our take: buy new, and buy the 2026. A used 2024 asks a median $44,714, only about $1,200 under what TrueCar says buyers pay for a new SR5 ($45,885). The 2022 to 2024 trucks carry NHTSA engine recalls, and used-loan rates average 11.19% against Toyota’s 1.99% on a new hybrid.

rows.when: Most buyers. Toyota’s financing, the $1,000 cash and the leases apply to the 2026, it costs $640 to $4,530 less than a 2027, and its ToyotaCare covers two years or 25,000 miles.
rows.check: That the truck is a 2026 and not a 2027, and that the offer runs in your region.

rows.when: The 2026 you want is gone, or you want the 14-inch touchscreen and built-in dash camera Toyota makes standard for 2027.
rows.check: The price rise, that its 3.99% and $1,000 cash run only in Southern California and the New York area, and that ToyotaCare drops to one year or 10,000 miles.

rows.when: You want a 2024 or 2025 with a warranty, and you’re paying cash.
rows.check: That it’s Gold Certified (7 years or 100,000 miles of powertrain cover from purchase), not Silver (12 months or 12,000 miles), and that every engine recall is done. A hybrid battery stays covered for 10 years or 150,000 miles from first sale.

rows.when: Your budget is under about $40,000; a 2022 asks a median $39,079.
rows.check: Open recalls by VIN, above all the engine campaigns on 2022 to 2024 trucks, and an independent inspection.

after: If you buy a 2022, 2023 or 2024 Tundra, get the engine recall work in writing. Toyota has recalled certain 2022 to 2024 trucks with the 3.4-liter V35A engine because manufacturing debris can damage the main bearings and stall the engine; the fix is a main-bearing inspection and, where needed, a new engine, free of charge. Engine is the most-cited component in NHTSA’s owner complaints for those years (166 of 436 on the 2022, 174 of 424 on the 2023, 158 of 365 on the 2024).

watch: Engine recalls on 2022 to 2024 trucks. Three NHTSA campaigns (24V381, 25V767 and 26V320) cover the V35A engine’s main bearings. Ask the dealer to show that each applicable one is done before you take delivery.
The Toyota Financial Services requirement. The rates and leases need Toyota’s own financing, and the $1,000 cash doesn’t combine with them. Compare the total cost with your bank’s rate.
The model year. A 2026 and a 2027 look alike on the lot. In Chicago and Dallas only the 2026 has offers.
Fuel economy. Edmunds measured 15.2 mpg on its test route against the EPA’s 19 for a 4WD Tundra. Budget for the real figure if you tow or drive in town.

Towing and payload. Toyota’s top figures are 12,000 pounds and 1,850 pounds, and Edmunds says buyers who tow or haul near the limit should look at the F-150 and Silverado. Check the rating for your exact cab, bed and engine on the door sticker.
Add-ons and fees. Ask for an itemized out-the-door price and refuse anything you didn’t ask for. Destination is $2,195 on top of every MSRP on this page.
faq: Is the Toyota Tundra a good truck?

Reviewers mostly say yes, with caveats. U.S. News gives the 2026 a 9.0 and third of six full-size pickups, J.D. Power’s owner score is 82 (quality and reliability 82, resale 90), and Kelley Blue Book’s expert rating is 4.1 out of 5. Edmunds is cooler at 7.0, fourth of five large trucks, and faults its fuel economy, its thick front pillars and mid-pack towing. A Tundra loses 19.7% of its value in five years by iSeeCars’ figures, against 37.0% for full-size pickups.
How much under MSRP can you get a Toyota Tundra?

On a 2026 SR through 1794 Edition, 5–7% under MSRP is a fair deal and 8–9% a strong one. The Capstone has a little more room, and the TRD Pro sells near sticker, around 3–4%. Those ranges are our read of TrueCar’s averages, Edmunds’ suggested prices and CarWhere’s verified buyers, so a given dealer may land a point either side. Toyota’s $1,000 cash comes on top of the discount, but not with its low rates.
Should I buy a 2026 or a 2027 Tundra?

The 2026, for most buyers. It costs $640 to $4,530 less, nearly all of Toyota’s offers are on it, and its ToyotaCare runs two years against one on the 2027. The 2027 adds a standard 14-inch touchscreen and a built-in dash camera, and it gets 3.99% and $1,000 cash in Southern California and the New York area only.
What is the destination charge on a Tundra?
$2,195. Toyota’s advertised starting prices leave it out, so a $41,260 SR is $43,455 on the window sticker.
Does Toyota offer cash back on the Tundra?

Yes: $1,000 customer cash on 2026 gas and i-FORCE MAX trims, except the TRD Pro, in all four regions we checked on November 18, 2026. It doesn’t combine with Toyota’s 1.99% or 2.99% financing or its leases, and a $500 military rebate and a $500 college rebate are listed separately.
Is the Tundra i-FORCE MAX hybrid worth it?

Only if you want its power. It makes 437 hp and 583 lb-ft against 389 hp and 479 lb-ft, but it adds $3,700 to a Limited and is rated 20 mpg combined against 19 in 4x4. Toyota’s best financing rate (1.99%) reaches it in all four regions we checked, which helps the monthly cost. Edmunds describes the hybrid as more about power than fuel economy.
Is a used Tundra a better deal than new?

Rarely. CarWhere’s median asking price for a used 2024 is $44,714 and for a 2025 $50,489, while TrueCar’s average paid for a new 2026 SR5 is $45,885. Used loans averaged 11.19% in the second quarter of 2026, against Toyota’s 1.99% on a new hybrid. A 2022 to 2024 truck needs its engine recalls checked; a Gold Certified 2024 or 2025 with them done is the used route we’d take.

vehicles.name: Mazda CX-5
vehicles.title: Mazda CX-5 Price: MSRP, Discounts and What to Pay | Steer Me Right
vehicles.description: What a Mazda CX-5 costs in November 2026: MSRP by trim for the new-generation 2026 and 2027 CX-5, how far under sticker dealers sell it, Mazda’s current offers, and the trim we’d buy.
vehicles.h1: Mazda CX-5 price: what to pay and how far under MSRP to aim
vehicles.summary: The CX-5 was redesigned for 2026, and it’s a roomier, calmer compact SUV that dealers are willing to discount. Edmunds found the back seat expansive, the ride smooth and the cabin quiet, U.S. News ranks it first of 14 compact SUVs, and IIHS lists it as a Top Safety Pick+. The catches: there’s no hybrid yet, so it’s rated 26 mpg combined, and Edmunds clocked 9.0 seconds to 60 mph, among the slowest small SUVs it has timed. Edmunds scores it only 6.5 out of 10, 14th of 20, because the driving feel went soft and most controls moved onto the touchscreen. Supply is generous, too: Edmunds counts about 27,300 new CX-5s and a median 57 days to sell one, against 34 for the average new vehicle, and its Texas suggested prices run 4–5% under sticker. Price a 2026 Preferred, aim for 4–5% under MSRP, and ask whether the dealer’s quote uses Mazda’s 0% financing or its $1,000 customer cash, because you can’t have both. Prices and offers were checked on November 18, 2026.

after: Destination is $1,595 on both model years ($1,640 in Alaska) and comes on top of every figure above. The 2027 costs $150 to $550 more on every trim but the base 2.5 S, with the same engine; its Gemini voice assistant replaces the Google Assistant that early 2026s launched with. Mazda’s October 26 release says 2027s reach dealers “in the coming months,” and Mazda’s site now shows only the 2027. Edmunds and Kelley Blue Book still print a $1,495 destination charge, so their sticker totals read $100 low. Equipment is from Mazda’s 2027 release; Edmunds’ trim notes match it for the Select and Preferred.

pick: A 2026 2.5 S Preferred. At $34,250 it costs $2,260 more than a Select, and the step up buys heated front seats and a heated steering wheel, a power liftgate, a 10-way power driver’s seat with memory, 19-inch wheels and a color head-up display. Edmunds’ own pick is the Select, but it says to splurge on the Preferred if you live somewhere cold, and it lists the Preferred as the most popular trim. Mazda’s $1,000 customer cash covers the S, Select and Preferred.

Pick the Select ($31,990) if price comes first: it adds leatherette seats and wireless CarPlay to the base car. Skip the Premium: its panoramic roof, leather and Bose audio cost $2,650 more than a Preferred. Take the Premium Plus only for the 15.6-inch screen and 360-degree camera; it’s also the only trim whose headlights IIHS rates Good.

intro: CX-5s are plentiful. Edmunds counts about 27,300 new ones for sale and says they take a median 57 days to sell, against 34 for the average new vehicle. Its suggested prices, built from Texas sales through November 2, run 5.1–5.3% under sticker on the S, Select and Preferred and 3.9–4.2% under on the Premium and Premium Plus. Kelley Blue Book’s fair purchase price is $1,385 to $1,585 under MSRP (3.6–5.0% by trim), CarWhere’s 18 verified buyers paid a median 5% under (the middle half 3–7.3%), and iSeeCars puts dealer invoice 2.5% under MSRP.

rows.why: Edmunds’ Texas prices run 5.1–5.3% under and Kelley Blue Book’s 4.0–5.0%. Mazda’s $1,000 customer cash comes separately.
Edmunds’ Texas prices run 3.9–4.2% under and Kelley Blue Book’s 3.6–3.7%. New York also lists $1,000 bonus cash on these two.

pay.note: Our estimate, checked November 18, 2026, on the 2026. Edmunds’ and Kelley Blue Book’s figures include a $1,495 destination charge, $100 under Mazda’s $1,595; CarWhere’s 5% is against MSRP.

choice.text: Each bar is how much less you pay in total than at the 6.35% average new-car rate, on a $34,000 CX-5 over 36 months. The $1,000 customer cash can’t be combined with the 0% rate, so the bars show which is worth more. Borrowers with top credit averaged 4.41%, so get your bank’s rate before you sign.

intro: Our take: buy new, and buy the 2026. A used 2025 costs about $3,200 less than a discounted new base car, but it’s the smaller, previous-generation CX-5, and Mazda’s 0% financing or $1,000 cash narrows the gap. CarWhere’s median used 2025 asks $26,669 at about 30,500 miles, while Edmunds’ Texas price for a new 2.5 S is $29,875 with destination. Used loans average 11.19% against Mazda’s 0%.

rows.when: Most buyers. It has Mazda’s 0% APR and customer cash, and plenty of stock.
rows.check: Which Mazda offer the quote uses, and that the car is a 2026. Google built-in is free for a year, and Edmunds puts the subscription after that at $15 a month.

rows.when: Mazda’s 2.9% rate covers only the 2027 where you live, or the color or trim you want is only on a 2027.
rows.check: The $150 to $550 price rise on every trim above the base, and whether the dealer has one yet.

rows.when: You want a CX-5 from the last several years with a warranty.
rows.check: That it’s Mazda Certified, not a dealer’s own program. Mazda lists a 160-point inspection, a 12-month/12,000-mile limited warranty and a 7-year/100,000-mile limited powertrain warranty. Ask the dealer for the age and mileage limits.

rows.when: Your budget is under about $24,000.
rows.check: Open recalls by VIN, an independent inspection, and the engine complaints on 2019 and 2021 cars.

after: If you buy used, a 2022 to 2025 CX-5 is the safer bet than a 2019 or 2021. NHTSA logged 277 owner complaints on the 2019 (134 about the engine) and 150 on the 2021 (81 about the engine), against 66 for the 2022, 67 for the 2023, 47 for the 2024 and 29 for the 2025. NHTSA’s lookup showed no recalls on 2020 to 2026 CX-5s on November 18, and two on the 2019 (engine stalling and a cracking fuel pump). Check any used CX-5’s open recalls by VIN.

watch: Offers that don’t stack. Mazda’s $1,000 customer cash can’t be combined with its special APR or lease. Ask the dealer for the price with each, and compare the total cost with your bank’s rate.

The model year. A 2026 and a 2027 look alike on the lot. The 2027 costs $150 to $550 more on every trim above the base, and Mazda’s 2.9% rate in Chicago, Dallas and New York is on the 2027 only, while the 0% is on the 2026.

Touchscreen controls. Edmunds says the physical buttons were replaced by touchscreen controls and that the steering wheel’s touch-sensitive panels didn’t always register presses. Try the climate and cruise controls on a test drive, with the screen in use.
The data plan. Google built-in is free for one year through Mazda Connected Services, then needs a monthly subscription (Edmunds says $15).
The destination charge. Mazda’s is $1,595. Edmunds and Kelley Blue Book print $1,495, so check the window sticker against any quote.
Headlights below the top trim. IIHS rates the Premium Plus headlights Good and every other trim’s Acceptable.

Early owner complaints. NHTSA has 20 on the 2026 so far, mostly about the electrical system (6), forward collision avoidance (4) and wipers or visibility (3). Edmunds’ owner summary mentions screen problems and warning lights.
Small-item storage and towing. Edmunds finds no extra shelves or cubbies and a small center bin, and rates towing at only 1,500 pounds.
faq: Is the Mazda CX-5 a good car?

Reviewers split. U.S. News scores the 2026 a 9.3 out of 10, first of 14 compact SUVs, while Edmunds rates it 6.5, 14th of 20 small SUVs, and calls it less engaging to drive than before. Kelley Blue Book’s owners give it 4.2 out of 5 (6 reviews), IIHS lists it as a Top Safety Pick+, and iSeeCars counts 20.0% of its value lost in three years, against 24.8% for the average vehicle.
How much under MSRP can you get a Mazda CX-5?

On a 2026 S, Select or Preferred, 4–5% under MSRP is a fair deal and 6% or more a strong one; on the Premium and Premium Plus, 3–4% is fair. Those ranges are our read of Edmunds’ Texas prices (5.1–5.3% under on the lower trims), Kelley Blue Book’s fair purchase prices and CarWhere’s 18 verified buyers (a median 5% under), so a given dealer may land a point either side. Mazda’s $1,000 customer cash is separate.
Should I buy a 2026 or a 2027 CX-5?

The 2026, for most buyers. It’s the same engine and equipment for $150 to $550 less on every trim above the base, and it carries Mazda’s 0% APR and customer cash. Buy the 2027 if Mazda’s rate covers only the 2027 where you live (the 2.9% rate in Chicago, Dallas and New York) or you want one before the 2026s run out.
Is there a CX-5 hybrid?
Not yet. Every 2026 and 2027 CX-5 has a 2.5-liter four-cylinder. Mazda says additional powertrain options will be announced in 2027, and Edmunds expects a hybrid to arrive then.
What mpg does the CX-5 get?
The EPA rates every 2026 CX-5 at 26 mpg combined (24 city/30 highway). All-wheel drive is standard, so there’s no front-drive version to compare.
What is the destination charge on a CX-5?
$1,595 ($1,640 in Alaska) on the 2026 and 2027, per Mazda’s releases. Mazda’s advertised starting prices leave it out, and Edmunds and Kelley Blue Book still print $1,495.
Does Mazda offer cash back on the CX-5?

Yes. In Chicago, Dallas, Los Angeles and New York on November 18, 2026, Mazda offered $1,000 customer cash on a 2026 S, Select or Preferred, on top of 0% financing in three regions and loyalty and military cash. The customer cash can’t be combined with Mazda’s special APR or lease.
Is a used CX-5 a better deal than new?

Only if you want to spend under about $24,000. CarWhere’s median asking price for a used 2025 is $26,669 at about 30,500 miles, and Edmunds’ Texas price for a new 2026 2.5 S is $29,875 with destination. A used 2025 is also the smaller, previous-generation CX-5, and used loans averaged 11.19% in the second quarter of 2026.

vehicles.description: What a Ram 1500 costs in November 2026: MSRP by trim for 2026 and 2027, how far under sticker dealers sell it, Ram’s employee pricing and cash, and whether to buy new, used or CPO.
vehicles.h1: Ram 1500 price: what to pay and how far under MSRP to aim
vehicles.summary: The Ram 1500 is the full-size pickup to buy for ride and cabin rather than towing numbers, and November is a good month to buy one. Edmunds scores it 7.5 out of 10 and says it rides more comfortably than any rival, thanks to rear coil springs. The catches are towing (up to 11,610 pounds, against 13,500 for the F-150 at Kelley Blue Book) and reliability, which Edmunds scored 3 out of 10 after its long-term test truck’s electronic problems. Dealers are well stocked: Cox counted 148 days of supply for Ram against 87 for the industry, and Ram is offering employee pricing to everyone plus up to $6,750 of cash on a 2026 through November 30. Aim 8–10% under MSRP on most trims (our estimate), take the Laramie’s turbo six over the V8, and price Ram’s 0% financing against its cash. Prices and offers were checked on November 18, 2026.

after: Prices leave out the $2,795 destination charge. Each price is Ram’s starting price for the cab Ram’s compare page lists first. A 5.7L HEMI V8 (395 hp) is optional on many trims. For 2027 every trim above rises $400 to $550 except the RHO, which rises $1,200. The 2027 also adds the Rumble Bee ($61,990 on Ram’s page) and the TRX SRT ($99,995).

pick: A 2026 Laramie Crew Cab, with 4x4 if you see snow. At $61,480 (4x2) it brings the standard 420-hp turbo six, heated and ventilated leather seats and the 12-inch screen, and Edmunds names it the editors’ pick of the 1500 range. Edmunds clocked a turbo six to 60 mph in 5.2 seconds against 6.9 for the V8, and calls the six quieter and cheaper. A Laramie also gets the broad $5,250 cash offer in Chicago, Dallas and New York ($6,750 in Los Angeles), or 0% financing for 60 months.

If you want to spend less, a Big Horn Crew Cab 4x4 starts at $53,430 and has the biggest cash on the list, $6,000 (only on the oldest 30% of eligible dealer stock). Skip the V8 and the Limited and Tungsten unless you want the 540-hp engine or the seats. Edmunds timed the 540-hp truck to 60 mph in 4.7 seconds, but a Limited costs about $15,000 more than a Laramie.

intro: Rams don’t sell at sticker. Cox counted 148 days of supply for Ram at the end of October against 87 for the industry, and Edmunds says new 2026 Ram 1500s are taking 126 days to sell against 34 for the average new vehicle. Edmunds’ November tips put the average buyer about $4,400 under MSRP (7–8%), CarWhere’s 59 verified 2026 buyers paid a median 9.1% under, and Kelley Blue Book’s fair purchase prices run 5–10% under. Edmunds’ suggested prices, based on Texas sales through November 2 and including destination, run 17–20% under its MSRP on every trim except the RHO (10.6%), because Ram’s cash and employee pricing are large this month.

rows.why: Kelley Blue Book’s fair purchase price is 7–8% under. Ram’s cash is $1,500 to $4,000 on these trims. Dealer invoice sits 4% under.

pay.note: Discount ranges are our estimate from Edmunds, Kelley Blue Book, CarWhere and iSeeCars’ invoice figures, checked November 18, 2026. They count Ram’s employee pricing and cash, so a trim without that money sits at the low end.

addons.title: Military, or a first responder?
addons.text: Ram takes $500 off select 2026 and 2027 trucks for active, reserve and retired military and veterans within 12 months of discharge, and $500 for law enforcement officers, firefighters and EMTs. Ask your dealer whether it stacks with the cash.

choice.title: 0% costs about {gap} less than the average loan
choice.text: Each bar is how much less you pay in total than at the 6.35% average new-car rate, on a $67,000 Laramie over 60 months. Ram’s 0% can’t be combined with its cash or, by its own disclosure, any other offer, so it also gives up employee pricing, which the cash bar keeps but doesn’t count. Borrowers with top credit averaged 4.41%, so get your bank’s rate and price both deals.

intro: Our take: buy new, and buy the 2026. A 2026 comes with Ram’s cash or 0%, and Ram’s dealers are carrying the most stock of any brand but Jeep. A used 2024 asks a median $37,898 and a 2025 $40,566, close to what Edmunds’ Texas suggested price puts on a new Big Horn ($42,883), and used loans average 11.19% against Ram’s 0% on a new one.

rows.when: Most buyers. Employee pricing, bonus cash, 0% financing and the 10-year powertrain warranty offer all apply to the 2026, and it costs $400 to $1,200 less than a 2027.
rows.check: That the truck is a 2026, that the cash is for that exact trim and cab in your ZIP, and that you take delivery by November 30.

rows.when: The 2026 you want is gone, or you want a 2027-only version such as the Rumble Bee or TRX SRT.
rows.check: The price rise ($400 to $550, $1,200 on the RHO), and that Ram shows only employee pricing and 5.9% financing on it in Chicago, with no cash.

rows.when: You want a 2023 to 2025 with a warranty and don’t mind buying through a dealer.
rows.check: Ram’s terms are a 125-point inspection, a 3-month/3,000-mile Maximum Care warranty and 7-year/100,000-mile powertrain coverage with a $100 deductible. Ram’s page gives no age or mileage limit, so ask the dealer.

rows.when: Your budget is under about $33,000.
rows.check: Open recalls by VIN, an independent inspection, and on a 2019 to 2022 whether the seat belt anchorage recall 26V495 and the tailgate hinge recall 22V904 are done.

after: If you buy used, get the recall work in writing. Recall 26V495 (second-row seat belt anchorage) covers 2019 to 2026 trucks, 25V298 (driver’s air bag) covers 2019 to 2024, and 24V653 (anti-lock brake software) covers 2019 and 2021 to 2024. The 2019 trucks drew 1,505 NHTSA complaints and the 2020 to 2022 trucks 645 to 692 each, against 211 for 2023 and 79 for 2024.

watch: Which cash you get. Ram’s cash differs by trim, cab and bed, and by region. The $6,000 on a Big Horn is limited to the oldest 30% of eligible dealer inventory. Ask which tier the exact truck is in.
Delivery by November 30. Every 2026 offer needs delivery by that date, and the 2026 is the model year with the cash.
0% or cash, not both. Ram’s 0% disclosure says it can’t be combined with other offers. Price the truck both ways and compare the total.

Reliability. Edmunds scored the Ram 3 out of 10 on reliability after its one-year test truck had numerous electronic problems, and J.D. Power’s owners rate quality and reliability 73 of 100, which it calls average. Electrical system is the top NHTSA complaint component on the 2019, 2020 and 2023 to 2026 trucks.
The model year. A 2026 and a 2027 look alike on the lot. Most offers are on the 2026, and the 2027 costs more.
Recalls. Ask the dealer to show that every open recall is done, especially 26V495 and the 2026 headlight, air bag and tire pressure recalls (26V421, 26V622, 26V623).
faq: Is the Ram 1500 a good truck?

Reviewers rate it highly for comfort. Edmunds gives the 2026 a 7.5 out of 10 and says it rides more comfortably than any rival; Kelley Blue Book scores it 4.5 out of 5 from its experts; U.S. News gives it 9.5 and second of six full-size pickups. Edmunds scored its reliability 3 out of 10, J.D. Power’s owner score is 74, and the Ford F-150 scores 83.
How much under MSRP can you get a Ram 1500?

On most 2026 trims, 8–10% under MSRP is a fair deal and 12% or more is a strong one, and the Laramie to Tungsten group runs 7–9% fair. The RHO has the least room, about 5–6%. Those ranges are our estimate from Edmunds, Kelley Blue Book, CarWhere and iSeeCars’ invoice figures, and a given dealer may land a point either side.
Should I buy a 2026 or a 2027 Ram 1500?

The 2026, for most buyers. It costs $400 to $1,200 less, and Ram’s cash and 0% financing apply to it through November 30. The 2027 gets employee pricing and a 5.9% rate in Chicago. Edmunds counts more 2027 trucks in stock (about 42,400) than 2026s (about 36,300).
What is the destination charge on a Ram 1500?
$2,795 on both years. Ram’s advertised starting prices leave it out, so a $42,025 Tradesman is $44,820 on the window sticker.
Does Ram offer cash back on the 1500?

Yes, on the 2026. In Chicago, Dallas and New York the cash is $1,500 to $5,250 depending on trim, with $6,000 on a Big Horn Crew Cab 4x4. Los Angeles pays up to $6,750. Employee pricing comes with the cash, and 0% financing replaces both. The 2027 shows no cash.
Is the V8 or the turbo six better?

The six. In Edmunds’ tests the 420-hp six reached 60 mph in 5.2 seconds and the 395-hp V8 in 6.9, and Edmunds calls the six quieter and cheaper. The V8 returns in 2026, and Kelley Blue Book calls it the gem of the line on towing and price. The 540-hp six does it in 4.7 seconds.
Is a used Ram 1500 a better deal than new?

Rarely. CarWhere’s median asking price for a used 2024 is $37,898 and for a 2025 $40,566, while Edmunds’ Texas suggested price for a new Big Horn is $42,883. Used loans averaged 11.19% in the second quarter of 2026, against Ram’s 0% on a new one. A certified 2023 to 2025 with its recalls done is the used route we’d take.

vehicles.name: Hyundai Elantra
vehicles.title: Hyundai Elantra Price: MSRP, Discounts and What to Pay | Steer Me Right
vehicles.description: What a Hyundai Elantra costs in November 2026: MSRP by trim for the gas, Hybrid and N, how far under sticker dealers sell it, Hyundai’s current offers, and the trim we’d buy.
vehicles.h1: Hyundai Elantra price: what to pay and how far under MSRP to aim
vehicles.summary: The Elantra is the compact sedan to cross-shop against the Civic and Corolla when price and space matter: it starts $1,870 below a Civic LX before destination, Edmunds calls it one of the most spacious small sedans (rear seat especially), and the Hybrid Blue is rated 54 mpg combined against 50 for a Corolla Hybrid. Hyundai covers the powertrain for 10 years or 100,000 miles, and IIHS names it a 2026 Top Safety Pick. The catches: Edmunds timed the base 147-hp car at 9.4 seconds to 60 mph, slower than average for small sedans, and finds wind noise high; iSeeCars counts 16.6% of its value lost in three years against 12.1% for compact cars. It sells well under sticker, too: Edmunds’ Texas prices run about 6% under with destination, and Hyundai adds $2,000 bonus cash on the gas car until November 30. Hyundai showed the next-generation Elantra in South Korea in June 2026, and the U.S. launch is expected in 2027, so a 2026 is the last of this design. Price a 2026 SEL Sport Premium, aim for 3–4% under MSRP, and take Hyundai’s 3.49% financing if your bank can’t beat it. Prices and offers were checked on November 18, 2026.

after: Hyundai’s starting prices leave out the $1,295 destination charge, which iSeeCars and Edmunds’ trim prices confirm. Hyundai lists no 2027 Elantra: the redesigned model was shown in South Korea in June 2026 and is expected in U.S. showrooms in 2027, with U.S. prices not yet announced. The Elantra N has its own prices in the Elantra N section below. Kelley Blue Book still prints the older $23,870 for an SE (its freight figure is $1,245), so some sites show lower sticker prices than Hyundai’s current list.

pick: A 2026 SEL Sport Premium. At $25,275 it costs $1,325 more than an SEL Sport, and Hyundai lists Smart Cruise Control with Stop & Go (adaptive cruise control: it holds a set gap to the car ahead and resumes after a stop), heated front seats and the version of automatic emergency braking that watches for oncoming cars when you turn left, none of which are on the SEL Sport. It’s rated 34 mpg combined, and it’s a gas car, so it qualifies for Hyundai’s $2,000 bonus cash and 3.49% financing this month. Edmunds’ pick is the $27,375 Limited, which adds dual 10.25-inch screens, leatherette seats and Bose audio; step up if you want those.

Pick the Hybrid Blue ($25,650) if fuel economy decides it: it’s rated 54 mpg combined against 34, about 130 fewer gallons a year at 12,000 miles, for $1,700 more than an SEL Sport. This month Hyundai gives only $500 and 3.9% on the hybrid. Skip the SE unless price is everything, and skip the N Line unless you want the 201-hp turbo: Edmunds finds it quicker and sportier, but it’s very scarce.

intro: Elantras sell under sticker, and Hyundai adds money on top this month. intro: Our take: buy new, and buy the 2026. The 2026 is the last of this design, Hyundai is paying $2,000 on the gas car, and a used one barely costs less: CarWhere’s median used 2025 asks $21,235 at about 26,700 miles, while Edmunds’ Texas price for a new 2026 SE is $22,700 with destination. Used loans average 11.19% against Hyundai’s 3.49%.

rows.when: Most buyers. It gets the $2,000 bonus cash, 3.49% financing and the 10-year/100,000-mile powertrain warranty.
rows.check: That Hyundai’s cash and rate cover the trim you want (the Hybrid and N get less), and that recalls 26V692000 (front struts) and 26V693000 (wheel bearings) are done.

rows.when: You don’t need a car before 2027 and want the new design, a larger screen and the redesigned hybrid.
rows.check: That Hyundai hasn’t announced U.S. prices or an on-sale date, and that a new design usually costs more than a closeout.

rows.when: You want a 2021 to 2026 with a warranty. Hyundai’s 5.99% helps.
rows.check: That it’s Certified Used, not Select Used. Certified adds a 173-point inspection, 5 years/60,000 miles of comprehensive cover and a transferable 10-year/100,000-mile powertrain warranty from first sale; Select Used gives only 90 days or 5,000 miles of powertrain cover.

rows.when: Your budget is under about $17,000.
rows.check: Open recalls by VIN, an independent inspection, and the engine on a 2019 or 2020 (the top complaint category on both).

after: If you buy used, look at a 2023 or newer Elantra. The 2023 drew 118 NHTSA owner complaints, the 2024 58 and the 2025 36, against 253 for the 2019 and 255 for the 2020, where engine problems led the list (135 and 109). The 2021 and 2022 have the most recall campaigns (6 and 7). Check any used Elantra’s open recalls by VIN.

watch: Dealer add-ons. CarWhere found add-ons on 34.1% of the 5,211 verified quotes it studied, averaging $1,454 (it doesn’t break out Hyundai). Paint protection, nitrogen and etched VINs are the dealer’s products. Refuse or negotiate them.

The wheel and strut recalls. NHTSA recall 26V693000 covers some 2026 Elantras, Elantra Hybrids and Elantra Ns whose lug nuts may loosen so a wheel can detach (Hyundai replaces the hub bearings; owner letters are expected in December). 26V692000 covers loose front strut fasteners on some 2026 Elantras. Ask the dealer to show both are done.
Which trims the cash covers. The $2,000 is for the gas Elantra. The Hybrid gets $500 and the N none. Hyundai’s fine print for the Hybrid’s $500 names different trims in different regions.
Hyundai financing. The college rebate needs Hyundai Motor Finance, and in Dallas so does the $2,000. Compare the total cost with your bank’s rate.
Wireless phone connection. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto come only with the 8-inch screen; the larger 10.25-inch screen needs a cable, Edmunds found.
The next Elantra. Hyundai has shown a redesigned Elantra for 2027 and hasn’t priced it for the U.S.
faq: Is the Hyundai Elantra a good car?

Most reviewers rate it well for value. U.S. News scores the 2026 a 9.0 out of 10, fourth of eight compact cars, and its Hybrid a 9.2 (third of nine hybrid cars, and a 2026 Best Compact Hybrid Car for the Money). Edmunds rates the gas car 6.8 and the Hybrid 7.6, Kelley Blue Book 4.6 out of 5 and J.D. Power owners 83 out of 100. Edmunds says the base engine is slow and the cabin loud, and its owner reviews average 3.5 out of 5. iSeeCars counts 16.6% of its value lost in three years, against 12.1% for compact cars.
How much under MSRP can you get a Hyundai Elantra?

On a gas SE through Limited, 3–4% under MSRP is a fair deal and 5–6% a strong one; the N Line and the hybrids differ (see the table). Those ranges are our read of Edmunds’ Texas prices (about 6% under), its November tips, Kelley Blue Book’s fair prices and iSeeCars’ invoice figures, so a given dealer may land a point either side. Hyundai’s $2,000 bonus cash on the gas car comes on top.
Is the Elantra Hybrid worth the extra money?

If you drive a lot. A Hybrid Blue is $1,700 more than a gas SEL Sport and is rated 54 mpg combined against 34, about 130 fewer gallons a year at 12,000 miles. This month Hyundai gives $500 and 3.9% on the hybrid against $2,000 and 3.49% on the gas car, which narrows the gap in the gas car’s favor. Edmunds says hybrids sell in a median 16 days.
Does the Hyundai Elantra have a redesign coming?

Yes. Hyundai showed the next-generation Elantra in South Korea in June 2026, and Kelley Blue Book reports it’s expected in U.S. showrooms in 2027. We found no U.S. prices or on-sale date, so a 2026 is the current car.
What is the destination charge on an Elantra?
$1,295 on the 2026. Hyundai’s advertised starting prices leave it out: the SE’s $22,825 is $24,120 with destination.
Does Hyundai offer cash back on the Elantra?

Yes on the gas car. On November 18, 2026, Hyundai offered $2,000 bonus cash on the gas Elantra, $500 on the Hybrid and none on the N, through November 30. There’s also $500 for military buyers and for recent graduates.
Is the Elantra N worth buying?

Edmunds ranks it first of four sport compacts (7.1 out of 10), and U.S. News scores it 9.4, second of six. It starts at $35,300, less than a GR Corolla ($40,520) or Civic Type R ($47,395). See the Elantra N section for how it differs.
Is a used Elantra a better deal than new?

Rarely this month. CarWhere’s median asking price for a used 2025 is $21,235, and Edmunds’ Texas price for a new 2026 SE is $22,700 with destination, plus $2,000 of Hyundai cash. Used loans averaged 11.19% in the second quarter of 2026, against Hyundai’s 3.49%. A Certified Used 2023 to 2025 is the route we’d take.

spotlight.heading: Elantra N: the 276-hp one
intro: The Elantra N is a different car from the rest of the line: a 276-hp turbocharged 2.0-liter four with 289 lb-ft of torque, a six-speed manual or an eight-speed dual-clutch automatic, and an electronically controlled limited-slip differential driving the front wheels. Edmunds ranks it first of four sport compacts (7.1 out of 10) and U.S. News second of six (9.4), and Edmunds clocked 0 to 60 mph in 5.5 seconds with the automatic and 6.4 with the manual. Its catches are a trunk of 14.2 cubic feet with a chassis brace that partly blocks the pass-through, no adaptive cruise control, and highway wind and road noise Edmunds finds above average.

vehicles.h1: Subaru Forester price: what to pay and how far under MSRP to aim
vehicles.summary: The Forester is the compact SUV for buyers who want standard all-wheel drive, 8.7 inches of ground clearance and a clear view out, and who’ll pay for the hybrid. The gas engine is the weak spot: Edmunds timed a Forester Sport at 9.2 seconds to 60 mph and scores the car 5.7 out of 10, well below U.S. News’ 8.6 and J.D. Power’s 84. The hybrid (194 hp, 35 mpg combined) is quicker by Edmunds’ account, but it trails an AWD Toyota RAV4 at 41 mpg and an AWD Honda CR-V hybrid at 37. IIHS names the Forester a 2026 Top Safety Pick+, and iSeeCars counts 13.3% of its value lost in three years against 24.8% for the average vehicle. It’s also easy to discount: Edmunds’ Texas prices run about 7% under sticker on every trim, and Cox counted 62 days of Subaru supply at the end of October, against 24 for the RAV4. Price a 2026 Premium Hybrid, aim for 5–6% under MSRP, and take Subaru’s 3.99% financing if your bank can’t beat it. Prices and offers were checked on November 18, 2026.

after: All-wheel drive is standard on every Forester. Destination is extra: $1,450 on the 2026 and $1,525 on the 2027. For 2027 Subaru dropped the gas Sport, Sport Onyx Edition and Touring, kept the Base, Premium and every hybrid at their 2026 prices, and added a Wilderness Hybrid at $40,495, the first Subaru Wilderness with a hybrid; it’s the one 2027 trim missing from this table. The 2027 Limited costs $1,600 more and the 2027 Wilderness $2,500 more, because equipment that was optional is now standard. The EPA’s 2027 listing rates the hybrid at 36 mpg combined, a point above the 2026. Subaru cut most 2026 prices on February 10, 2026, so some review sites still print older, higher figures; these are Subaru’s.

pick: A 2026 Premium Hybrid. At $34,730 it costs $2,735 more than a gas Premium, and the step buys the hybrid system (194 hp against 180, and 35 mpg combined against 29), 12.3-inch digital gauges, a power rear gate and blind-spot detection. A gas Premium sells the last two together as a $1,200 package, so the real gap is $1,535, and the EPA’s fuel-cost estimate ($1,700 a year against $2,050) pays it back in about four years. Edmunds calls the gas Forester slow, 9.2 seconds to 60 mph in its tested Sport, and says the hybrid is noticeably quicker. That alone is worth the money to us.

If you tow or drive unpaved roads, take the Wilderness ($36,995, Edmunds’ editors’ pick). It’s rated to tow 3,500 pounds against 1,500 for most Foresters and sits 9.3 inches off the ground, but it’s rated 26 mpg combined. Edmunds likes the gas Sport for value, but at $34,795 it costs $65 more than a Premium Hybrid and is rated 28 mpg combined. Skip it for the hybrid.

intro: Foresters sell about 7% under sticker. Edmunds’ Texas suggested prices run 6.8–7.4% under with destination on every trim, its November tips say buyers are paying about $2,600 below MSRP on average, and CarWhere’s five verified buyers paid a median 7.3% under MSRP. iSeeCars puts dealer invoice 6.1–6.9% under MSRP. Supply is ample: Edmunds counted about 27,100 new Foresters in stock and Cox 62 days of Subaru supply at the end of October, against 87 for the industry. Even so, Edmunds says Foresters sell in a median 16 days, so the scarcer trims may not move much. Kelley Blue Book’s fair purchase price for a Base is $1,845 under its $31,445 MSRP with destination, about 5.9%.

intro: Our take: buy new, and buy the 2026. A used Forester costs about what a discounted new one does: CarWhere’s median asking price for a 2025 is $31,476 at about 15,000 miles, while Edmunds’ Texas price for a new 2026 Premium is $31,124 with destination. Subaru’s 1.99% and 3.99% rates are on the 2026 only, used loans average 11.19%, and the 2027 adds $75 to destination.

rows.when: Most buyers. Subaru’s rates and leases are on the 2026, destination is $75 less, and the gas Sport, Sport Onyx Edition and Touring exist only as 2026s.
rows.check: That the car is a 2026, and that recalls 26V685 (ball joint), 26V346 (moonroof glass) and 25V889 (rear hatch bracket) are done if it’s on them.

rows.when: You want the Wilderness Hybrid ($40,495), which exists only for 2027, or a Limited or Wilderness with the power rear gate and heated steering wheel standard. Subaru said the 2027 arrives at retailers later this fall.
rows.check: The higher gas Limited and Wilderness prices ($1,600 and $2,500 more), the $1,525 destination charge, and whether any 2027 offer exists yet (none was listed).

rows.when: You want a recent used Forester with a warranty. Subaru lists finance rates from 4.29%.
rows.check: That it’s Subaru Certified: a 152-point inspection, a 7-year/100,000-mile powertrain agreement with a $0 deductible, 24/7 roadside assistance and a history report. Subaru’s page doesn’t give age or mileage limits, so ask.

rows.when: Your budget is under about $27,000. CarWhere’s median 2023 asks $26,997 at about 35,000 miles.
rows.check: Open recalls by VIN, an independent inspection, and for a 2025 or 2026, that the recalls above are done.

after: If you buy used, look at a 2023 or 2024 Forester and skip the 2019 and 2020. Those two drew 834 and 604 NHTSA owner complaints, 370 and 252 of them in NHTSA’s visibility and wiper category, against 77 for the 2023 and 32 for the 2024. The 2024 has two recalls (loose engine water pipe bolts, a driveshaft that can crack), both free fixes. The redesigned 2025 drew 104 complaints in its first year, 13 of them about forward collision avoidance, and has three recalls. Check any used Forester’s open recalls by VIN.

watch: The ball-joint recall. NHTSA recall 26V685, filed October 19, 2026, covers some 2026 Foresters whose left-front lower control arm ball joint may separate. Subaru tells owners not to drive an affected car until the dealer has fixed it. Ask whether the car you’re buying is on it, and get the repair in writing.
Which engine you test-drive. Edmunds finds the gas Forester slow and its engine coarse and noisy when you push it. Drive the hybrid and a gas car back to back on a highway on-ramp before you pick.

Dealer add-ons. Paint protection, nitrogen and etched VINs are the dealer’s products. Refuse or negotiate them, and ask for a written quote that lists MSRP, your discount and each fee on its own line.
The option package on a gas Premium. The power rear gate and blind-spot detection that come standard on the Premium Hybrid are a $1,200 package on a Premium. Add it before you compare the two.
The 2027’s changes. A 2026 and a 2027 look alike on the lot. The 2027 has a $1,525 destination charge, costs more on the gas Limited and Wilderness, and loses the gas Sport and Touring.

The credit conditions. Subaru’s 1.99% and 3.99% are for well-qualified buyers, need delivery from retailer stock by November 30, and the 3.99% covers only the Premium, Sport, Limited and Touring Hybrids. Compare the total cost with your bank’s rate.
faq: Is the Subaru Forester a good car?

Reviewers like it but don’t agree how much. U.S. News scores the 2026 an 8.6 out of 10, eighth of 14 compact SUVs, and J.D. Power owners give it 84 out of 100, second in the class. Edmunds rates it 5.7 out of 10 and calls the gas engine slow, Kelley Blue Book gives it 4.4 out of 5, and IIHS names it a 2026 Top Safety Pick+. iSeeCars counts 13.3% of its value lost in three years, against 24.8% for the average vehicle.
How much under MSRP can you get a Subaru Forester?

About 5–6% on most 2026 trims, and 7% or more on a strong deal. Those ranges are our read of Edmunds’ Texas prices (6.8–7.4% under sticker on every trim), CarWhere’s five verified buyers (a median 7.3% under) and iSeeCars’ invoice figures, so a given dealer may land a point either side. The Base and Sport Hybrid are tighter on supply, so 4–5% is fair. Subaru has no cash back to add on top.
Is the Forester Hybrid worth it?

For most buyers, yes. A Premium Hybrid costs $2,735 more than a gas Premium, or $1,535 after counting the $1,200 package the gas car needs for a power rear gate and blind-spot detection. It’s rated 35 mpg combined against 29, and the EPA estimates $1,700 a year in fuel against $2,050. Edmunds says the hybrid is noticeably quicker. It still trails an AWD Toyota RAV4 hybrid (41 mpg combined) and an AWD Honda CR-V hybrid (37).
Should I buy a 2026 or a 2027 Forester?

The 2026, for most buyers. Subaru’s 1.99% and 3.99% financing is on the 2026, its destination charge is $75 less ($1,450 against $1,525), and the Base, Premium and hybrid trims cost the same either year. Buy the 2027 if you want the new Wilderness Hybrid ($40,495), or a Limited or Wilderness with more standard equipment, and don’t mind paying $1,600 or $2,500 more for it.
Is the Forester good off-road?

More than most small SUVs. Every Forester has all-wheel drive and at least 8.7 inches of ground clearance. The Wilderness adds 9.3 inches, all-terrain tires, underbody protection, a full-size spare and a 3,500-pound tow rating, which Edmunds calls the one to get if you tow. Other Foresters tow 1,500 pounds.
What is the destination charge on a Forester?
$1,450 on the 2026 ($1,600 in Alaska) and $1,525 on the 2027 ($1,675 in Alaska); Subaru says it may vary in CT, HI, MA, ME, NH, NJ, NY, RI and VT. Subaru’s advertised starting prices leave it out.
Does Subaru offer cash back on the Forester?

No. In Chicago, Dallas, Los Angeles and New York on November 18, 2026, Subaru listed 1.99% and 3.99% financing and two lease deals, but no customer cash. The only money off is a $500 military discount.
Is a used Forester a better deal than new?

Rarely. CarWhere’s median asking price for a 2025 is $31,476 at about 15,000 miles, and Edmunds’ Texas price for a new 2026 Premium is $31,124 with destination. Used loans averaged 11.19% in the second quarter of 2026, against Subaru’s 1.99% or 3.99% on a new one. A Subaru Certified Forester is the used route we’d take.

vehicles.h1: Chevrolet Colorado price: what to pay and how far under MSRP to aim
vehicles.summary: The Colorado is the midsize pickup to price if you tow: Chevrolet rates it to pull 7,700 pounds against the Ford Ranger’s 7,500, and Edmunds scored its towing and hauling 10 out of 10. It isn’t the roomiest or the most reliable truck in the class. Edmunds and U.S. News fault the back seat, and Consumer Reports expects it to be less reliable than the average new car. It does sell well under sticker: Edmunds’ Texas suggested prices run 7–10% under, with about 18,900 trucks in stock and 40 days to sell. Price a 2026 LT, aim for 6–7% under MSRP, and take Chevrolet’s 4.9% financing if your bank can’t beat it. Prices and offers were checked on November 18, 2026.

pick: A 2026 LT crew cab, with 4WD if you leave pavement. At $36,000 for the 2WD (4WD adds $3,300) it adds the EZ Lift and Lower tailgate with built-in storage and remote start to the WT, and Edmunds names it the editors’ pick of the lineup. Chevrolet’s $1,000 customer cash applies to it (the Trail Boss and ZR2 get $500), and Edmunds’ Texas prices show it selling 10.0% under sticker, the deepest of any trim.

If you’ll use trails, a Trail Boss costs $1,200 more than an LT 4WD ($40,500 against $39,300) and adds a 2-inch lift, 32-inch all-terrain tires and a two-speed automatic transfer case, which Chevrolet lists on the Trail Boss and which U.S. News says some other trims lack. rows.check: CarBravo’s certified warranty is 12 months/12,000 miles bumper to bumper on trucks under 10 model years and 100,000 miles. Chevrolet’s own powertrain warranty runs 5 years/60,000 miles from first sale, by Edmunds’ account.

rows.when: Your budget is under about $34,000: a 2023 asks a median $33,399.
rows.check: Open recalls by VIN and an independent inspection. A 2021 or 2022 (median asks $24,830 and $24,995) is the previous generation; the Colorado was redesigned for 2023.

after: If you buy a 2023 or 2024, ask for the recall paperwork. Those trucks were recalled for a camera fault that could trigger automatic emergency braking (the truck brakes on its own) by mistake, overtightened front wheel hub bolts and a loose seat belt buckle bolt, and the 2024 for mismatched tires and a fuel pump lock ring that could leak fuel in a crash.

watch: Brakes. NHTSA is running an engineering analysis (EA26006) into loss of brake assist on GM vehicles with the eBoost brake system, and the 2023 to 2026 Colorado is on its list. No recall had been issued as of November 18, 2026. Ask the dealer to check the VIN for open recalls and read the brake complaints on NHTSA before you buy.
Cash or rate. Chevrolet lists the $1,000 cash and the 4.9% rate as separate offers and doesn’t say whether they combine. Ask for a quote each way and compare the total cost.
The model year. A 2026 and a 2027 look alike on the lot, and the cash and financing are on the 2026.

The back seat. Edmunds says the rear seats lack comfort and taller riders may lack knee room, and U.S. News calls the back seat tiny and says loading a child seat is a pain. Sit in it with your own seat.
Storage and controls. Edmunds scores storage 3 out of 10 (small door pockets) and says the headlight controls sit in the touchscreen. Try both on the lot.
Fees and add-ons. Dealers add fees and extras to the price you see online. Compare out-the-door prices, and refuse or negotiate anything you didn’t ask for.
faq: Is the Chevrolet Colorado a good truck?

Reviewers rate it well but not at the top. Kelley Blue Book gives it 4.6 out of 5 (third among midsize trucks), U.S. News 8.7 and third of seven, and J.D. Power’s owner score is 83, second behind the Tacoma’s 84. Edmunds is cooler at 6.5, fourth of seven, and faults the rear seat and storage. Consumer Reports expects it to be less reliable than the average new car, and iSeeCars puts its five-year value loss at 36.9% against 30.2% for midsize pickups.
How much under MSRP can you get a Chevrolet Colorado?

On a 2026 WT, Custom or LT, 6–7% under MSRP is a fair deal and 9–10% a strong one. The Trail Boss and Z71 run 6–7% fair and 8–9% strong, and the ZR2 has less room, around 5–6%. Those ranges are our read of Edmunds’ Texas suggested prices, Kelley Blue Book’s fair purchase prices and iSeeCars’ invoice figures, so a given dealer may land a point either side, and Chevrolet’s cash comes on top.
Should I buy a 2026 or a 2027 Colorado?

The 2026, for most buyers. It costs $100 to $1,200 less, and Chevrolet’s 4.9% financing and customer cash are on the 2026. The 2027 has a 350-hp engine against 310, which matters if you tow near the 7,700-pound limit. The only 2027 offer we found is the $2,000 conquest cash.
What is the destination charge on a Colorado?
$2,095 on both model years. Chevrolet’s advertised starting prices leave it out, so a $32,400 WT is $34,495 on the window sticker.
Does Chevrolet offer cash back on the Colorado?

Yes. On November 18, 2026 it listed $1,000 customer cash on a 2026 (Trail Boss and ZR2 get $500), $1,000 for eligible military members, and $2,000 conquest cash for owners of a 2012 or newer Tacoma, Ranger, Ridgeline, Frontier, Bronco, Gladiator or Wrangler, per GM Authority. All run to November 30. Chevrolet’s page doesn’t say which combine.
Should I buy a Colorado or a Tacoma?

Buy the Colorado if you tow or want more standard power and a bigger screen: Edmunds says its towing, payload and screen lead the class. Buy the Tacoma if resale matters most. It loses 19.5% of its value in five years against the Colorado’s 36.9% (iSeeCars), owners score it 84 against 83 at J.D. Power, and Edmunds calls it the safe choice in the segment. If you own a Tacoma, Chevrolet’s $2,000 conquest cash lowers the Colorado’s price.
Is a used Colorado a better deal than new?

Rarely. CarWhere’s median asking price for a used 2024 is $36,087 and for a 2025 $38,636, while a new 2026 LT starts at $36,000 and sells 6–7% under that, with 4.9% financing against 11.19% for the average used loan. A certified 2023 to 2025 with its recalls done is the used route we’d take.

vehicles.h1: Hyundai Tucson price: what to pay and how far under MSRP to aim
vehicles.summary: The Tucson is the compact SUV to price if you want the most equipment and the longest warranty for the money, and the hybrid is the one to look at. U.S. News scores it 9.3 out of 10 and ranks it first, tied with the Mazda CX-5, among compact SUVs, and Edmunds says it costs about what a Honda CR-V or Toyota RAV4 does while giving you more features. Even the $29,700 SE has a 12.3-inch touchscreen with wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, and every Tucson carries a 10-year/100,000-mile powertrain warranty. The catches: Edmunds timed the gas engine at 10.2 seconds to 60 mph, one of the slowest crossovers it has tested; the Hybrid’s 38 mpg combined trails the CR-V Hybrid’s 40 and the RAV4’s 43; and it loses value faster than most (iSeeCars: 24.8% in three years for the gas Tucson and 29.2% for the Hybrid, against 22.7% for compact SUVs). It sells well under sticker, too: about 40,800 new Tucsons are in stock, and Edmunds’ Texas prices run 5.7–7.5% under. Hyundai says an all-new Tucson arrives in early 2027, so a 2026 is the last of this generation. Price a 2026 Hybrid SEL Convenience, aim for 3–4% under MSRP, and take Hyundai’s 0% or 2.9% financing if your bank can’t beat it. Prices and offers were checked on November 18, 2026.

Hyundai had posted no 2027 prices on November 18, 2026: it lists an all-new Tucson for early 2027. Some review sites still print older figures (U.S. News lists a $29,200 SE); these are hyundaiusa.com’s.

pick: A 2026 Hybrid SEL Convenience. At $35,250 it costs $2,500 more than a front-drive Hybrid SEL, and the step up buys 12.3-inch digital gauges, leatherette seats, ambient lighting and a wireless charging pad, with all-wheel drive included (a Hybrid SEL with AWD is $34,250, so the real gap is $1,000). It’s rated 36 mpg combined, about 130 fewer gallons a year at 12,000 miles than an AWD gas SEL Premium (26 mpg, and $300 more at $35,550). Edmunds also picks it among the hybrids, calling the hybrid far quicker than the gas engine and about 10 mpg thriftier.

Pick the Hybrid SEL ($32,750, front-drive) if price comes first: it’s rated 38 mpg combined and keeps heated seats and a power driver’s seat. Skip the Hybrid Limited and Night: they cost $7,175 and $7,675 more than the Convenience, and Edmunds says they sell fastest, so you’ll have less room to negotiate. Skip the plug-in unless you can charge at home: the $40,675 SEL goes about 32 miles on electricity, and Hyundai quotes $1,665 and up to install a home charger.

intro: Tucsons sell under sticker, and there’s plenty to choose from. Edmunds counted about 40,800 new Tucsons nationwide and says they sell in about 25 days, against 34 for the market. Its Texas suggested prices run 5.7–7.5% under sticker with destination (a $29,201 SE against $31,350; a $32,047 Hybrid SEL against $34,400), though its November tips say about $1,200 off MSRP on average, with no general customer rebates. TrueCar’s page shows buyers paying 1.9% less than MSRP across the Tucson line (our read of TrueCar was blocked, so that figure is from a search-result summary), and iSeeCars puts dealer invoice 4.0% under MSRP on the gas SE through SEL Premium, 5.0% on the Limited and 3.4% on every hybrid. CarWhere has too few verified 2026 Tucson purchases to publish a typical discount.

intro: Our take: buy new, and buy the 2026. A used Tucson saves you less than it seems: CarWhere’s median asking price for a 2025 is $24,493 at about 31,000 miles, while Edmunds’ Texas suggested price for a new 2026 SE is $29,201 with destination, and Hyundai finances the new one at 0% or 2.9% against an 11.19% average for used loans. The all-new Tucson is due in early 2027 with no U.S. price yet, which is a reason to wait only if you want the redesign.

rows.when: Most buyers. Hyundai’s 0% and 2.9% rates and Edmunds’ prices 6–7% under sticker apply to it, and about 40,800 are in stock.
rows.check: That the offer covers the 2026 and the trim you want, and that the car’s open recalls are done (see below).

rows.when: You want the redesign and can wait until early 2027. Hyundai calls it all-new, with a next-generation hybrid system.
rows.check: That price and mpg are published before you commit; Hyundai had posted neither on November 18, 2026.

rows.when: You want a 2021 to 2025 with a warranty. Hyundai’s 5.99% for up to 60 months applies to select cars.
rows.check: That it’s Certified (a 173-point inspection, a 5-year/60,000-mile comprehensive warranty, a 10-year/100,000-mile powertrain and hybrid battery warranty), not the cheaper Select Used program.

rows.when: Your budget is under about $22,000.
rows.check: Open recalls by VIN, an independent inspection, and on a 2019 to 2021 that recall 20V543 was done.

after: If you buy used, look at a 2023 or 2024 Tucson and check the recalls: the 2024 has four (one covers power steering that can lose assist), the 2023 two. Skip the 2019 to 2021 unless recall 20V543 (an ABS control unit that can short and start an engine-compartment fire; the fix is a fuse) was done; those years drew 387, 180 and 85 NHTSA complaints, many of them filed under the engine. The 2022 drew 505. The 2025 drew 455, 220 of them about forward collision avoidance, and it has seven recalls, including 25V549 (connecting rod bolts; Hyundai replaces the engine) and 26V316 (a camera software fix for sudden automatic braking). Check any used Tucson’s open recalls by VIN.

watch: Open recalls on 2025 and 2026 Tucsons. NHTSA lists six on the 2026: 25V549 (connecting rod bolts that can cause loss of drive power; Hyundai replaces the engine on affected cars), 26V316 (front camera software that can brake the car suddenly), 26V047 and 26V400 (instrument display software), 26V254 (side-impact sensors) and, on the 2026 Hybrid only, 26V692 (front strut fasteners that can cost steering control). Ask for the VIN’s recall status before you sign.

The bonus cash needs Hyundai financing. On the gas SEL Premium and Limited, Hyundai’s fine print says to finance through Hyundai Motor Finance and apply the cash as a down payment. Get your bank’s rate first, then compare the total.

The all-new Tucson. Hyundai says it arrives in early 2027. A 2026 you buy now is the last of this generation, so ask the dealer for the out-the-door price in writing and compare it across two or three stores.

All-wheel drive on the hybrid. The SEL Convenience, Limited and Night come with it and are rated 36 mpg combined; a front-drive Hybrid SE or SEL is rated 38. A Hybrid SEL with AWD costs $1,500 more than front-drive.
A slow gas engine. Edmunds timed an AWD gas Limited at 10.2 seconds to 60 mph and found the eight-speed clunky unless you drive gently. The hybrid’s extra power is the main reason to pay for it.
Dealer add-ons and fees. Dealer-installed extras and documentation fees come on top of the advertised price. Ask for an out-the-door quote and refuse or negotiate any add-on you didn’t pick.
faq: Is the Hyundai Tucson a good car?

Most reviewers rank it at or near the top of its class. U.S. News scores the 2026 a 9.3 out of 10, first in compact SUVs and tied with the Mazda CX-5, Edmunds scores it 7.9 and fourth of 20 small SUVs, and J.D. Power gives it 81. Edmunds’ complaints are a slow gas engine and a screen-only control layout. NHTSA gives it five stars overall.
How much under MSRP can you get a Hyundai Tucson?

On a gas SE through SEL Premium, 3–4% under MSRP is a fair deal and 5–6% a strong one, in our estimate from Edmunds’ Texas prices and iSeeCars’ invoice figures. A Limited has more room (4–5% fair, 6% or more strong); a Hybrid Limited or Night has less (2–3%, 4–5%). Hyundai’s bonus cash and 0% or 2.9% financing come on top.
Should I buy the gas Tucson or the Hybrid?

The Hybrid, for most buyers. Edmunds calls the gas engine one of the slowest crossover engines it has tested (10.2 seconds to 60 mph) and says the hybrid is quicker and gets about 10 more mpg. A Hybrid SEL Convenience is rated 36 mpg combined against 26 for an AWD gas SEL Premium and costs $300 less than that AWD SEL Premium ($35,250 against $35,550) and $1,200 more than a front-drive one.
Does Hyundai offer cash back on the Tucson?

Hyundai lists up to $3,000 in bonus cash on the gas Tucson, $1,750 on the Hybrid and $4,000 on the Plug-in. On the gas SEL Premium and Limited the fine print requires financing through Hyundai Motor Finance and applying the cash as a down payment; Edmunds says there are no general customer rebates. Ends November 30, 2026.
Is a new Hyundai Tucson coming?

Yes. Hyundai’s site lists an all-new Tucson and Tucson Hybrid for early 2027, with no U.S. price or mpg yet. The 2026 is the last of the current generation, introduced for 2022 and refreshed for 2025.
What is the destination charge on a Tucson?

$1,650, per iSeeCars’ trim table, which matches Hyundai’s own fine print on a Hybrid Night ($44,575 including destination against a $42,925 sticker). Hyundai’s MSRPs leave it out; Edmunds’ prices include it.
Is AWD worth it on a Tucson?

If you see snow. It adds $1,500 on the gas Tucson and the Hybrid SE and SEL, and costs about 2 mpg combined (28 to 26 on gas, 38 to 36 on the Hybrid SEL). The Hybrid SEL Convenience, Limited, Night and both plug-ins come with it.
Is a used Tucson a better deal than new?

Rarely. CarWhere’s median asking price for a used 2025 is $24,493, while Edmunds’ Texas price for a new 2026 SE is $29,201, and Hyundai finances the new one at 0% or 2.9% against 11.19% on average for used loans. A used 2023 or 2024 is the value play; certified ones carry Hyundai’s 5.99% rate.

vehicles.name: Ford Ranger
vehicles.title: Ford Ranger Price: MSRP, Discounts and What to Pay | Steer Me Right
vehicles.description: What a Ford Ranger costs in November 2026: MSRP by trim from the XL to the Raptor, how far under sticker dealers sell it, Ford’s current cash and financing offers, and whether to buy new, used or CPO.
vehicles.h1: Ford Ranger price: what to pay and how far under MSRP to aim
vehicles.summary: The Ranger is the midsize pickup to price first if ride quality and tech matter to you. Edmunds ranks it first of seven midsize trucks and timed a 4x4 Lariat to 60 mph in 6.7 seconds, a second quicker than a comparable Tacoma. The catch is the sticker: Edmunds says it costs a bit more than the Colorado, and U.S. News ranks it seventh of seven, citing low-speed transmission jitters and cheap cabin materials. Ford is carrying plenty of stock (112 days of supply across the brand in October, against 87 for the industry) and adds $2,000 cash plus $500 Black Friday bonus cash through November 30. Price a 2026 XLT, aim for 3–4% under MSRP before Ford’s cash, and get your bank’s rate before you accept Ford’s 4.9%. Prices and offers were checked on November 18, 2026.

after: Prices leave out the $1,895 destination charge. The 2027 prices are Cars.com’s, because Ford has not posted 2027 prices on ford.com; its Lariat is $1,230 below the 2026’s, and Ford has not said why. A report on Ford’s 2027 order guide says the 2.7L V6 gives way to a 3.0L V6 on the XLT and Lariat, which Ford has not confirmed.

pick: A 2026 XLT, 4x4 if you leave pavement, with the standard 2.3L four-cylinder. At $36,075 it costs $2,525 more than the XL and adds wireless phone charging and rear parking sensors, which Edmunds credits when it names the XLT its Editors’ Pick. The 4x4 adds $3,500. Ford’s lease deals are aimed at the XLT too.

If you tow, every trim with the Trailer Tow Package is rated at 7,500 pounds, so the V6 buys no extra capacity. Edmunds tested both engines and found the 2.7L V6 only a little quicker (6.2 seconds to 60 mph against 6.7 for the four-cylinder Lariat) and rated at 20 mpg combined against 21 with 4x4, so we’d skip it. The Raptor is a different truck: $57,270, 17 mpg combined and a 5,510-pound tow rating. Ford’s cash does not apply to it, and Edmunds says it sells about $800 under sticker.

intro: Rangers sell under sticker, and Ford’s cash comes on top. Edmunds’ November tips put the average buyer about $1,362 under MSRP before Ford’s $2,000 cash, and a Ranger sells in a median 22 days against 34 for the average new vehicle. Ford is long on trucks, though: Cox counted 112 days of supply for the brand in October against 87 for the industry. CarWhere’s 14 verified buyers paid a median 6.2% under MSRP, in a sample too small to lean on. The Raptor is the exception, with about $800 off and no general cash.

rows.why: Edmunds’ average is about $1,362 under MSRP before cash, and iSeeCars’ dealer invoice sits 3–4% under. CarWhere’s median buyer got 6.2% under.

intro: Our take: buy new, and buy the 2026. A used 2024 asks a median $37,075, about what a new XLT costs before Ford’s $2,500 cash, and used loans average 11.19% against Ford’s 4.9% on a new one.

rows.when: Most buyers. Ford’s cash, financing and leases apply to the 2026, and it is the truck dealers are stocked with.
rows.check: That the offer runs in your region, that the truck is not a Raptor if you expect the bonus cash, and that its recalls are done.

rows.when: You can wait, or you want the 2027’s changes.
rows.check: Ford has not posted 2027 prices or offers on ford.com, and the 2027 lineup may swap the 2.7L V6 for a 3.0L V6, per a report on Ford’s order guide.

rows.when: You want a 2024 or 2025 with a warranty and you’re paying cash.
rows.check: That it is Gold Certified, not Blue. Gold covers trucks up to 6 years old with under 80,000 miles, adds a 172-point inspection, a 12-month/12,000-mile comprehensive warranty and 7-year/100,000-mile powertrain coverage. Blue Certified gives 90 days or 4,000 miles.

rows.when: Your budget is under about $31,000, which buys a 2023 or older.
rows.check: Open recalls by VIN, an independent inspection, and that you are comparing like with like: the Ranger was redesigned for 2024, so a 2023 is the previous generation.

after: Whichever you buy, ask for the recall paperwork in writing. NHTSA lists 13 recall campaigns on the 2024 and 13 on the 2025, and 8 on the 2026, including two engine recalls that can cause a loss of drive power.

watch: Engine recalls. NHTSA lists two recalls for loss of drive power on 2025 and 2026 Rangers. 26V343 (2025–2026) is fixed with a new engine long block; 26V548 (2026) is an inspection, and Ford’s letter says the remedy is expected in December 2026. Check any truck’s VIN before you sign.
Rearview camera recall. 26V605 covers 2026 Rangers with the 10.1-inch screen, which can lose power and drop the camera image. NHTSA lists the remedy as under development.

Dealer-installed extras. Ford’s own price list shows a hard roll-up tonneau cover at $1,470 and cargo management rails at $600. If a dealer’s quote includes extras you didn’t ask for, ask for them to come off.
The Raptor and the offers. The $500 bonus cash excludes the Raptor, and Edmunds says it carries no general cash. Don’t expect the Ranger deals to apply to it.
The model year. A 2026 and a 2027 can sit on the same lot. Ford’s current offers are for the 2026.
Financing terms. The 4.9% needs Ford Credit approval, and Ford’s pages do not say whether it combines with the cash. Compare the total cost with your bank’s rate.
faq: Is the Ford Ranger a good truck?

Most reviewers rate it well, with one outlier. Edmunds scores the 2026 a 7.1 out of 10 and ranks it first of seven midsize trucks, and Kelley Blue Book gives it a 4.7 out of 5. U.S. News scores it 8.4 and ranks it seventh of seven, and faults low-speed transmission jitters and cheap cabin materials. Consumer Reports expects about average reliability.
How much under MSRP can you get a Ford Ranger?

On an XL, XLT or Lariat, 3–4% under MSRP is a fair deal and 6–7% a strong one, before Ford’s $2,500 cash. The Raptor has less room, around 1–2%. Those ranges are our read of Edmunds’ tips, iSeeCars’ invoice figures and CarWhere’s 14 verified buyers, so a given dealer may land a point either side.
What is the destination charge on a Ranger?
$1,895 on the 2026. Ford’s advertised prices leave it out, so a $33,550 XL is $35,445 on the window sticker.
Does Ford offer cash back on the Ranger?

Yes, until November 30, 2026: $2,000 customer cash plus $500 Black Friday bonus cash on a 2026 Ranger, in Chicago, Dallas, Los Angeles and New York. The bonus cash is not available on the Raptor, and Edmunds says the Raptor has no general cash. Ford’s pages do not say whether the cash combines with its 4.9% financing, so ask the dealer.
Should I buy the 2.7L V6?

Probably not. Edmunds clocked a V6 Ranger at 6.2 seconds to 60 mph against 6.7 for a four-cylinder Lariat 4x4, found no towing gain, and the EPA rates the V6 at 20 mpg combined against 21 for the 2.3L 4x4. Both engines tow 7,500 pounds with the Trailer Tow Package.
Is the Ranger Raptor worth it?

Only if you will use it off pavement. It starts at $57,270 against $43,955 for a Lariat, is rated 17 mpg combined, and tows 5,510 pounds against 7,500. It makes 405 hp from a 3.0L twin-turbo V6, and gets none of Ford’s November cash.
Is a used Ranger a better deal than new?

Rarely. CarWhere’s median asking price for a used 2024 is $37,075 and for a 2025 $39,089, while a new XLT starts at $36,075 before Ford’s $2,500 cash. Used loans averaged 11.19% in the second quarter of 2026, against Ford’s 4.9% on a new one. A Gold Certified 2024 or 2025 with its recalls done is the used route we’d take.
